papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates TNBS-induced visceral pain and modulates cortical EEG rhythms in association with TREM1/DAP12 pathway inhibition: Enhanced effects with pharmacological TREM1 blockade.
papers.abstract: BackgroundVisceral pain in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) lacks effective therapies. Whether the TREM1/DAP12 pathway is associated with electroacupuncture (EA) analgesia and cortical EEG modulation remains unclear.ObjectiveTo determine if spinal TREM1/DAP12 is associated with EA's analgesic and neuromodulatory effects in TNBS-induced visceral pain.MethodsMale Sprague-Dawley rats with TNBS-induced colitis received EA (ST36/ST37), the TREM1 inhibitor Nangibotide, or their combination. Behaviors (PWT, CRD, DAI), spinal TREM1/DAP12, downstream inflammatory mediators, and microglial colocalization were evaluated. Cortical EEG was analyzed using normalized power spectral density (Normalized PSD, %).ResultsEA significantly alleviated visceral/referred hyperalgesia and reduced DAI scores (P < 0.05). TNBS upregulated spinal TREM1, DAP12, TNF-α, NLRP3, and TLR4 and increased TREM1/DAP12 microglial colocalization (P < 0.0001), all reversed by EA (P < 0.001). Nangibotide alone partially mimicked EA's effects, and their combination yielded greater analgesia and molecular suppression (P < 0.05). Normalized EEG analysis revealed that TNBS increased δ power (P < 0.0001) and reduced θ and β power (P < 0.001). Notably, EA and Nangibotide specifically reversed δ elevation and restored θ power (P<0.05) without altering β power (P > 0.05), with greater δ suppression than either treatment alone (P < 0.0001).ConclusionEA alleviates TNBS visceral pain and normalizes cortical δ/θ dysrhythmia, with these effects associated with suppression of microglial TREM1/DAP12 neuroinflammation. Pharmacological TREM1 blockade mimics and enhances EA's effects, supporting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for visceral pain.

papers.title: Supporting the driver's perception cognition action loop using an embodied intelligent cockpit framework for explainable fatigue intervention.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated a driver-support framework combining multimodal fatigue detection, feature attribution, and state-specific auditory feedback during conditional automated driving. Forty licensed drivers completed three counterbalanced 20-min simulator conditions: nonverbal warnings, generic speech, and explanatory speech. A fixed detector used electroencephalography (EEG), eye tracking, and vehicle dynamics. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) selected a dominant cue, which a large language model translated into a spoken message. Fatigue labels were based on the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale and a 60-s vigilance task. Braking reaction time, standard deviation of lane position (SDLP), and time-to-collision (TTC) exposure were assessed during manual driving following takeover. Compared with generic speech, explanatory speech was associated with a 0.192-s shorter mean braking reaction time (95% confidence interval: -0.223 to -0.161 s; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and a 0.085-m lower mean SDLP (95% confidence interval: -0.108 to -0.062 m; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). The mean proportion of time with TTC < 1.5 s was 0.07 versus 0.10. Retrospective leave-one-subject-out evaluation yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.85. The explanatory warning package was associated with faster braking and more stable lane keeping than generic speech in this simulator study. Further studies should separate message content from acoustic properties and assess performance in independent driving settings.

papers.title: Dietary Vitamin K2 Intake, Musculoskeletal Injury, and Cardiometabolic Health in Service Members.
papers.abstract: Vitamin K2 (K2) research has demonstrated that with sufficient K2 intake, vitamin K-dependent proteins are activated to regulate bone diseases and inflammation-related diseases, offering an innovative strategy to address ongoing musculoskeletal injury (MSKi) and high adiposity challenges that threaten health promotion, performance, and readiness in service members (SMs). This study aimed to characterize K2 status in a military sample and explore the relationship between dietary K2 intake and bone health, metabolic health, and inflammation status in the context of SM health and operational readiness or deployability. At baseline and 12 months, Army and Air Force units provided data from demographic and food frequency questionnaires, body composition, bone density, cardiometabolic, and biomarker measurements. Activity trackers monitored physical activity and sleep duration continuously. Between August 2023 and July 2024, we enrolled 47 active duty SMs. The sample was predominantly male, racially and ethnically diverse, averaged 27 years of age, and had an average of 6.5 years of service. At baseline, 45% met the criteria for stage I hypertension and 45% exceeded military body fat standards. Participants reported insufficient baseline dietary intake of vitamin K1+K2 and vitamin D. Over the 12 months, fermented food consumption slightly increased, activity behaviors remained unchanged, and participants self-reported 10 noncombat MSKis. Participants reported no significant changes in body composition, body fat specifically, or dietary intake of vitamin D or vitamin K2. Exploratory proteomics analysis identified links between K2 and inflammation, bone architecture, glucose homeostasis, and insulin receptors. MSKi, high body fat, and meeting optimal nutrition goals remain readiness challenges for SMs. Exploring K2 identified meaningful metrics and actionable strategies to address these challenges. Highlighting data-informed interventions adds to nursing's nutritional and cardiometabolic knowledge base and clinical interventions, as the nursing workforce is positioned to influence every step of patient care: conducting research, generating data to inform clinical practice and interventions, and ensuring evidence-based patient education and counseling to optimize SM health and readiness.

papers.title: CsLUX-CsPME6/CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 modulates pectin methylesterification to coordinate cold tolerance and growth in tea plants.
papers.abstract: Cell wall pectin methylesterification is critical for plant defense and development, yet how it coordinately regulates cold tolerance and growth in perennial crops remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that cold stress significantly reduces the degree of methylesterification (DM) of pectin in tea plants, concurrent with extensive remodeling of cellular and subcellular structures, including enhanced xylem development, altered mesophyll architecture, and impaired chloroplast morphology. Genome-wide analysis identifies 100 pectin methylesterase (PME) and 42 PME inhibitor (PMEI) genes, among which CsPME6, CsPMEI8, and CsPMEI17 exhibit cold-responsive expression and localize to the nucleus and apoplast. Functional studies demonstrate that CsPME6 positively regulates cold tolerance in tea plants, while CsPMEI8 and CsPMEI17 act as negative regulators. Mechanistically, CsPME6 elevates PME activity to lower pectin DM, whereas CsPMEI8 directly inhibit CsPME6 activity to maintain high pectin DM. Also, CsPMEI17 also negatively enhanced total PME activity to enhance the cold tolerance in tea plants. Notably, our findings suggested that the circadian clock component CsLUX directly binds to the LBS motifs in the promoters of these three genes, activating CsPME6 and repressing CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 expression, which contributes to pectin methylesterification homeostasis. Besides, CsLUX-CsPME6/CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 module also promote glutamate/γ-aminobutyric acid metabolism, leaf thickness, plant height, and root elongation in tea plants. Our findings underscore the importance of pectin methylesterification dynamics mediated by CsLUX-CsPME/PMEI involving cold tolerance and growth development in tea plants.

papers.title: Understanding the Link Between Eveningness and Depression: A Serial Mediation Study of Daytime Sleepiness and Pre-Sleep Arousal.
papers.abstract: The evening chronotype is consistently associated with depressive symptoms, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study examined whether daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal mediate the relationship between eveningness and depressive symptoms in adults. In this cross-sectional study, 524 adults were recruited from community health centers in Indonesia using convenience sampling. Chronotype, daytime sleepiness, pre-sleep arousal, and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Pre-Sleep Arousal Scale (PSAS), and Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS), respectively. Serial mediation analysis adjusted for age and gender was performed, with indirect effects tested using 5000 bootstrap resamples; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for caffeine consumption and sleep medication use. Participants with depressive symptoms had lower MEQ scores and higher ESS and PSAS scores than those without (all p < 0.001). Eveningness was associated with greater depressive symptoms both directly and indirectly through daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal. Eveningness retained a significant direct effect (69% of the total effect), indicating partial mediation. Pre-sleep arousal showed the strongest indirect effect (21.1% of the total effect), followed by the serial pathway through daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal (5.6%) and daytime sleepiness alone (4.3%). Results were similar after additional adjustment. Daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal partially mediated the relationship between eveningness and depressive symptoms, with pre-sleep arousal emerging as the strongest pathway. Interventions targeting bedtime hyperarousal may help reduce depressive symptoms in evening-type individuals, alongside approaches addressing other contributing mechanisms.

papers.title: Effect of Acoustic Environment Improvement Combined with Roy Adaptation Model-Based Supportive Nursing on Self-Efficacy and Maternal Role Adaptation in Advanced-Age Primiparas.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effect of acoustic environment improvement combined with Roy adaptation model (RAM)-based supportive nursing on self-efficacy and maternal role adaptation in advanced-age primiparas. This retrospective cohort study included 158 eligible advanced-age primiparas who gave birth in the obstetrics department of the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between February 2025 and February 2026. The primiparas were divided into a control group ( n = 80) and an observation group ( n = 78) according to the nursing method they actually received. The control group received RAM-based supportive nursing care, whereas the observation group received acoustic environment improvement combined with RAM-based supportive nursing care. The Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy scale, Maternal Role Adaptation Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), time to first lactation, and exclusive breastfeeding rate were compared between the two groups before and after nursing. Repeated-measures analysis of variance showed significant effects of time, group, and time × group interaction on maternal role adaptation scores (all P < 0.05). Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons demonstrated significant within-group changes over time (all adjusted P < 0.05), and the observation group had higher scores than the control group at discharge and 6 weeks postpartum (both P < 0.05). For PSQI scores, significant effects of time ( P < 0.001), group ( P = 0.003), and time × group interaction ( P = 0.039) were observed. The observation group showed lower PSQI scores than the control group at discharge and 6 weeks postpartum ( P = 0.004 and P = 0.001, respectively). Time to first lactation in the observation group was significantly shorter than that in the control group (24.87 ± 3.53 h vs. 28.21 ± 4.12 h; P < 0.001). At 6 weeks postpartum, the exclusive breastfeeding rate was significantly higher in the observation group than in the control group (76.9% vs. 62.5%; P = 0.049). Among advanced-age primiparas, acoustic environment improvement combined with RAM-based supportive nursing was associated with improved sleep quality, enhanced self-efficacy and neonatal care capabilities, and promoted maternal role adaptation, and may help promote lactation and increase the exclusive breastfeeding rate.

papers.title: Effects of Noise Reduction Management on Anxiety, Sleep Quality, and Early Postoperative Stress Responses in Patients After Thoracoscopic Lung Surgery.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of systematic noise reduction management on postoperative anxiety, sleep quality, and early stress responses in patients undergoing elective thoracoscopic lung surgery. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 150 patients who underwent elective thoracoscopic lung surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University in 2025. Patients were divided into a control group ( n = 75) receiving routine nursing care and an observation group ( n = 75) additionally receiving systematic noise reduction management. Anxiety (Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, SAS), sleep quality (Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire, RCSQ), heart rate variability (HRV) indices (standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals [SDNN], root mean square of successive differences [RMSSD], and low-frequency/high-frequency ratio [LF/HF]), and stress markers (serum cortisol [Cor], C-reactive protein [CRP], and procalcitonin [PCT]) were compared between groups at 1 day before surgery and at 1 and 6 days after surgery. Daytime, nighttime, and 24-hour noise levels were significantly lower in the observation group than in the control group (all P < 0.01). At 1 day after surgery, SAS scores increased and RCSQ scores decreased in both groups, with no significant intergroup differences ( P > 0.05). At 6 days after surgery, the observation group had significantly lower SAS scores (52.67 ± 5.21 versus 55.33 ± 6.85, P = 0.008) and higher RCSQ scores (48.45 ± 6.54 versus 40.87 ± 5.92, P < 0.001). Serum Cor, CRP, and PCT increased in both groups at day 1 and decreased by day 6, when they were significantly lower in the observation group (Cor 380.80 ± 42.79 versus 402.45 ± 32.43 nmol/L, P < 0.001; CRP 39.56 ± 6.33 versus 48.34 ± 7.89 mg/L, P < 0.001; PCT 0.12 ± 0.06 versus 0.15 ± 0.08 ng/mL, P = 0.017). HRV indices decreased at day 1 and recovered by day 6, when SDNN, RMSSD, and LF/HF were significantly higher in the observation group (all P < 0.01). Systematic noise reduction management was associated with lower anxiety levels, improved sleep quality, and attenuated early postoperative stress responses after thoracoscopic lung surgery, supporting its value as an adjunct to routine nursing care.

papers.title: Occupational Health Outcomes Among Staff Working in Low-, Medium-, and High-Noise Zones of the Central Sterile Supply Department and Operating Room.
papers.abstract: To explore the associations between noise exposure and occupational health indicators among staff working in the central sterile supply department (CSSD) and operating room. This cross-sectional observational study included 100 healthcare technicians working in the CSSD and operating room between January 2025 and February 2026. Based on the noise monitoring data of the hospital, the work zones were categorized into low-noise zone (<65 dB), medium-noise zone (65-75 dB), and high-noise zone (>75 dB) according to the equivalent continuous sound levels. Outcomes included hearing discomfort, tinnitus, sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI]), attentional performance (Digit Cancellation Test), mental fatigue (Mental Fatigue Scale), perceived workload (the NASA Task Load Index [NASA-TLX]), and thermal discomfort. A binary logistic regression model was used to analyze the association between noise exposure levels and occupational health outcomes. Compared with staff working in the low-noise zone, those working in high-noise zones had a higher incidence of hearing discomfort and tinnitus ( P < 0.05), and higher PSQI scores ( P < 0.01). High-noise exposure was significantly associated with poorer attentional performance and greater mental fatigue ( P < 0.01). The NASA-TLX total score in the high-noise zone was significantly higher than that in the low-noise zone ( P < 0.01), with the greatest differences observed in mental demand and temporal demand dimensions. In binary logistic regression analysis, staff working in high-noise zones had higher odds of tinnitus (OR = 3.82, 95% CI: 1.92-7.61, P < 0.001) and hearing discomfort (OR = 4.25, 95% CI: 2.11-8.56, P < 0.001). Higher occupational noise exposure was associated with hearing discomfort, poorer sleep quality, greater mental fatigue, poorer attentional performance, and higher perceived workload among staff working in CSSDs and operating rooms.

papers.title: Latent Profile Analysis of Psychosocial Adjustment and Subjective Noise Annoyance in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy.
papers.abstract: To identify latent profiles of psychosocial adjustment and subjective noise annoyance in patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR) and to analyze disease-related factors. This cross-sectional survey included 198 patients with DR. Participants completed the Psychosocial Adjustment to Illness Scale-Self Report (PAIS-SR), a subjective noise annoyance rating, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), and the Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Latent profile analysis was performed using the PAIS-SR domain scores and subjective noise annoyance scores as indicators. Multinomial logistic regression was used to identify demographic and disease-related factors associated with profile membership. Three profiles were identified: a well-adjusted profile (35.4%), an intermediate-adjustment profile (41.9%), and a high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile (22.7%), with an entropy of 0.922. Patients in the high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile had poorer sleep quality, higher anxiety levels, and lower social support than those in the other profiles, with significant differences in PSQI, SAS, and SSRS scores across the three profiles (all P < 0.001). Multinomial logistic regression showed that longer diabetes duration, proliferative DR, and poorer worse-eye best-corrected visual acuity were associated with membership in the less favorable profiles. For the high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile, the corresponding odds ratios (ORs) were 1.138, 3.599, and 1.259, respectively. Diabetic macular edema showed a borderline association with this profile (OR = 2.455, P = 0.050). Psychosocial adjustment and noise annoyance patterns are heterogeneous among patients with DR. Identifying patients with a high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile may support noise management and stratified nursing care.

papers.title: Effects of Noise Reduction Combined with AI-Based Nursing System on Postoperative Sleep Quality and Delirium Incidence in Older Patients with Severe Glioma.
papers.abstract: To explore the effect of noise reduction combined with the artificial intelligence (AI)-based nursing system on postoperative care in older patients with severe glioma. This retrospective analysis included 100 older patients with severe glioma admitted to Zhoukou Orthopedic Hospital between October 2020 and December 2025. Patients were assigned to the combined nursing group and the control group according to different nursing methods. Sleep quality, the incidence and duration of delirium, the incidence of postoperative complications, and nursing satisfaction were compared between the two groups at 7 and 14 days after surgery. At 7 and 14 days after surgery, the total and each dimension score of the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire in the combined nursing group were significantly higher than those in the control group ( P < 0.05). The combined nursing group had a lower incidence of delirium (7.27% versus 26.67%) and a shorter duration of delirium than the control group (both P < 0.05). The combined nursing group also had a lower incidence of postoperative complications (5.45% versus 22.22%) and a higher nursing satisfaction rate (96.36% versus 77.78%) than the control group (both P < 0.05). After adjustment for potential confounders, noise reduction combined with the AI-based nursing system was associated with significantly lower odds of postoperative delirium compared with routine care alone (OR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.78, P = 0.019). The combined intervention of noise reduction and AI-based nursing system was associated with a more favorable postoperative prognosis among older patients with severe glioma. It may help optimize postoperative nursing strategies for this patient population, although further verification is warranted.

papers.title: Effects of Noise Exposure on Sleep Quality and Dyspnea Perception in Hospitalized Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: To prospectively investigate the effects of noise exposure on sleep quality and dyspnea perception in hospitalized chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients. 128 COPD inpatients (January 2024 to December 2025) at the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University were enrolled. A portable sound level meter continuously monitored noise intensity for 72 h. Patients were divided into low (≤45 dB, n = 37), medium (46-60 dB, n = 65), and high (>60 dB, n = 26) noise exposure groups. Sleep quality was assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), dyspnea by the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scale and Borg scale. The high exposure group had significantly higher PSQI total scores (18.71 ± 3.82 versus 13.75 ± 3.36 versus 6.36 ± 0.84, P < 0.001), higher proportion of mMRC scores of 3-4, and higher Borg scores (rest: 4.38 ± 1.03 versus 3.26 ± 0.92 versus 2.17 ± 0.84; post-activity: 7.12 ± 1.34 versus 5.74 ± 1.26 versus 4.29 ± 1.13, all P < 0.05). Noise intensity positively correlated with PSQI score ( r = 0.782, P < 0.001) and Borg score ( r = 0.683, P < 0.001). Multivariate linear regression analysis further demonstrated that noise exposure intensity (per 10 dB increment) was independently associated with both PSQI total score ( B = 2.45, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.98-2.92, β = 0.68, P < 0.001) and post-activity Borg score ( B = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.08-1.96, β = 0.58, P < 0.001), after adjusting for age, Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease grade, disease duration, and hypnotic drug use. Higher noise exposure is associated with poorer sleep quality and more pronounced dyspnea perception in hospitalized COPD patients. Effective noise control measures should be implemented.

papers.title: Effects of Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle Nursing Combined with Noise Management on Sleep and Clinical Outcomes in Children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia Complicated by Encephalitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle nursing combined with noise management on sleep indicators and clinical outcomes during hospitalization among children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) complicated by encephalitis. A retrospective analysis was conducted. A total of 100 children were classified into an observation group and a control group according to the nursing care actually received during hospitalization, with 50 children in each group. The control group received routine nursing care, whereas the observation group received PDCA cycle nursing combined with noise management in addition to routine nursing care. Baseline characteristics, sleep quality indicators, clinical improvement outcomes, biomarker indices, and the incidence of complications were compared between the two groups. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between the two groups. After nursing care, the observation group had longer total sleep duration [8.0 (7.0, 8.5) h versus 7.5 (7.0, 8.0) h, P = 0.019], fewer awakenings [2.0 (1.0, 3.0) versus 3.0 (2.0, 4.0), P = 0.005], and fewer crying/startle episodes [1.0 (0.0, 2.0) versus 2.0 (1.0, 3.0), P = 0.009]. Fever duration and time to cough relief were also shorter in the observation group ( P = 0.004 and P = 0.010). Several inflammatory, neurological injury-related, and cerebrospinal fluid indicators differed significantly after nursing care. The overall complication rate was lower in the observation group (26.00% versus 48.00%, P = 0.023). Compared with routine nursing alone, the addition of PDCA cycle nursing combined with noise management was associated with greater improvement in sleep during hospitalization, faster relief of clinical symptoms, and a lower overall incidence of complications in children with MPP complicated by encephalitis, suggesting its potential value in optimizing nursing management for this population.

papers.title: Effects of Personalized Noise Reduction Combined with Comfort Care on Pain and Negative Emotions in Patients with Acute Pancreatitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of personalized noise reduction combined with comfort care on pain, negative emotions, and sleep quality in patients with acute pancreatitis (AP) who are hospitalized. This retrospective study included 80 AP patients admitted between January 2022 and July 2025. The patients were divided into a comfort care group ( n = 39) receiving routine nursing care plus standardized comfort care, and a combined care group ( n = 41) additionally receiving personalized noise reduction management. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), the Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale (SQS), the EuroQol Five-Dimension Five-Level (EQ-5D-5L), and the Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire-18(PSQ-18) scores were compared before and after 7 days of care. Continuous variables were analyzed using independent samples t-test for between-group comparisons and paired t-test for within-group comparisons. Categorical variables were compared using the chi-squared test. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Before care implementation, VAS, SAS, SDS, SQS, and EQ-5D-5L scores showed no statistically significant differences between the two groups ( P > 0.05). After 7 days of care, VAS, SAS, and SDS scores in both groups were significantly lower than before care ( P < 0.05). After care, the combined care group showed significantly lower scores than the comfort care group ( P < 0.05). SQS and EQ-5D-5L scores in both groups were significantly higher than before care ( P < 0.05). After care, the combined care group showed significantly higher scores than the comfort care group ( P < 0.05). PSQ-18 scores on day 7 showed significantly higher patient satisfaction in the combined care group than in the comfort care group ( P < 0.05). Personalized noise reduction combined with comfort care is a more effective way of alleviating pain, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances in AP patients than comfort care alone. This approach enriches comprehensive nursing with individualized acoustic environment management. However, due to the retrospective design of this study, prospective randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Nonauditory Effects of Infrasound and Low-Frequency Noise in Humans: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: This systematic review aimed to assess the quality of evidence across studies on the nonauditory effects of infrasound (IS) and low-frequency noise (LFN) in adults, investigating physiological and psychological outcomes associated with such exposures. Studies were searched in eight databases from their earliest records up to March 2026. Outcomes assessed included annoyance and noise sensitivity, sleep disturbances, cardiovascular diseases, cognitive and mental health impairments, and other health-related disturbances. The quality of evidence for each outcome was assessed using an adapted Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. The review included 39 papers, predominantly cross-sectional designs (laboratory-based and real-life), with fewer cohort studies and only three randomized controlled trials. Exposure scenarios varied widely, encompassing wind turbine noise, traffic and community noise, occupational noise, and experimentally generated IS and/or LFN stimuli. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate for annoyance/sensitivity to very low for sleep disturbance, cardiovascular outcomes, cognitive performance, mental health, and general health disturbances. These ratings were influenced by the predominance of cross-sectional studies, high overall risk of bias, methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent findings, and indirectness across outcomes. The findings showed that annoyance and sensitivity were the only outcomes associated with exposure to IS/LFN, supported by moderate-quality evidence, suggesting that these subjective responses should be included in health impact assessments. For all other outcomes, the certainty of the evidence remains very low, highlighting the urgent need for well-designed longitudinal and experimental studies.

papers.title: Noise Pollution in Cement Manufacturing Industries: A Comprehensive Review of Environmental and Occupational Health Impacts and Mitigation Strategies.
papers.abstract: The process of cement production is a somewhat neglected yet considerable contributor to noise pollution both in the workplace and its surroundings, as it produces high-intensity noise through various activities such as crushing, grinding, and heating. In the paper that follows, recent literature concerning the sources and effects of noise pollution in cement production is analyzed, and the effectiveness of various noise mitigation strategies is assessed. Publications from 2015 to 2025 were reviewed, along with some prior publications, focusing on various noise sources, effects on workers and the environment, and noise mitigation strategies. Loudness in cement-producing plants is about 68.8-103.3 dB(A) and is continuous in nature, unlike other industries' processes, which are characterized by sound bursts only. Subsequent effects on job-related experiences and workers' functioning include negative effects on hearing ability, heart problems, sleep disorders, and stress, which increases considerably due to the mixture of loudness with dust and chemicals; noise impacts animals' behavior, communication, and habitat. Together, engineering controls, administrative controls, and spatial planning in facilities form a structured control hierarchy that has proven to be effective. However, its implementation is hampered by high cost and inconsistent regulation across regions of the world. Most of the evidence for the reliability of this approach comes from cross-sectional studies of single factories with scarce longitudinal data. Hence, noise pollution in the cement production process presents a major multi-faceted risk for employees, and to mitigate this risk effectively, coordinated engineering, administrative, and regulatory measures must be applied.

papers.title: Protocol for cell-type-specific circadian bioluminescence recording from mouse gut muscularis externa explants.
papers.abstract: Cell-type-specific circadian recording is essential for understanding tissue-level circadian organization. This protocol describes the generation of intestinal cell-type-specific PER2::CBG-LUC reporter mice, preparation of intestinal longitudinal muscle-myenteric plexus explants, long-term bioluminescence recording using photomultiplier-based photon counting system, and analysis of circadian phase and rhythmicity. The protocol also includes procedures to verify that ex vivo rhythms reflect the endogenous in vivo circadian phase. For complete details on the execution of this protocol, please refer to Magaña et al.1.

papers.title: Targeted gene therapy alleviates epilepsy and hyperexcitability in models of SCN2A deficiency.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic SCN2A loss-of-function (LoF) variants can cause severe, refractory epilepsy with limited treatment options. Existing Scn2a-LoF mouse models exhibit few spontaneous seizures, limiting the dynamic range needed to assess therapeutic efficacy. We therefore generated gene-trap Scn2a-deficient mice on the seizure-prone DBA/2J background. These mice experienced hundreds of spontaneous absence seizures per day, characterized by concurrent behavioral arrest and EEG spike-wave discharges (SWDs). Partial restoration of Scn2a expression reduced seizure burden. Electrophysiological analysis revealed impaired action potential waveforms yet increased repetitive firing, alongside coordinated downregulation of voltage-gated potassium channel genes, potentially contributing to hyperexcitability. Given the broad potassium channel downregulation and prior efficacy of KCNA1 gene therapy in refractory seizure models, we selected KV1.1 as a potential therapeutic target and used a drug-controllable adeno-associated virus (AAV) to express human KCNA1. We found that this intervention normalized elevated neuronal firing and reduced spontaneous seizure burden in Scn2a-deficient mice. Extending these findings to a human cell-based platform, AAV-mediated KCNA1 expression also reduced neuronal firing in human cortical organoids carrying a SCN2A-truncating variant identified in patients. Together, these findings provide proof of principle for drug-controllable KCNA1 gene therapy as a promising treatment avenue for epilepsy related to SCN2A LoF variants.

papers.title: Late electroencephalographic seizure-risk findings and restricted diffusion on magnetic resonance imaging as seizure-burden markers associated with neurological deficits after status epilepticus in a remote or chronic cohort.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether time-dependent electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure risk findings and restricted diffusion on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are associated with neurological outcomes after status epilepticus (SE), beyond seizure duration. This two-center observational study included consecutive SE patients from 2017 to 2025. We examined three seizure-related markers: seizure duration ≥ 30 min, a 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on a late EEG (performed the following day or later after SE onset), and SE-related restricted diffusion on MRI (peri-ictal diffusion-weighted imaging hyperintensity with reduced apparent diffusion coefficient values). Outcomes were overall neurological worsening and SE-attributable focal neurological deficits at discharge. Multivariable models included the three markers and age> 65 years, with further adjustment for stupor or coma at admission and third-line therapy. Of 440 patients with suspected SE, 297 had confirmed SE; 221 with an identified seizure focus formed the overall cohort; 127 with remote symptomatic SE or preexisting chronic focal epilepsy formed the remote or chronic cohort. Overall neurological worsening occurred in 96 patients (43.4%) and SE-attributable focal neurological deficits in 68 (30.8%). In univariable analyses, seizure duration ≥ 30 min was associated with both outcomes in the overall cohort. A 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on late EEG was associated with both outcomes in both cohorts, whereas high-risk findings on early EEG were not. In multivariable models including seizure duration, restricted diffusion was independently associated with both outcomes in both cohorts, most strongly with focal neurological deficits in the remote or chronic cohort (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 28.59, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 7.23-154.99). A 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on late EEG was independently associated with focal neurological deficits in the remote or chronic cohort (adjusted OR = 4.26, 95% CI = 1.35-14.24), whereas seizure duration ≥ 30 min was not independently associated with either outcome. High-risk late-EEG findings and restricted diffusion were associated with neurological deficits. These markers may complement seizure duration in estimating cumulative seizure burden and focal brain injury.

papers.title: Neuroprotective effects of ıdebenone and citicoline in experimental traumatic optic neuropathy: electrophysiological, histological, and biochemical assessments in a rat model.
papers.abstract: OBJECTıVE: This study aims to investigate the neuroprotective efficacy of idebenone and citicoline in a rat model of traumatic optic neuropathy (TON), induced by controlled optic nerve (ON) crush injury. MATERıALS AND METHODS: Forty male Wistar rats (250-300 g) were randomly assigned to four groups (n=10). TON was induced in Groups 1, 2 and 3 via right ON crush. Group 1 received no treatment; Group 2 received idebenone (50 mg/kg/day), and Group 3 received citicoline (1 g/kg/day) via a nasogastric tube, starting 24 h post-injury. Group 4 served as sham controls. Flash and pattern visual evoked potentials (fVEP, pVEP) were recorded at baseline, 48 h, and day 28. The flash and pattern VEP tests were performed using the MonPackONE device. Blood biomarkers (ischemia-modified albumin (IMA), total and native thiol) were analyzed, and histological evaluations included hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) monoclonal antibody immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: At day 2, VEP tests indicated delayed latency and decreased amplitude in Groups 1-3 versus the sham group. By day 28, Groups 2 and 3 showed significant VEP improvement over Group 1. Biochemical analysis demonstrated higher thiol levels in Group 3 compared to Group 2 on day 28; however, this difference was not statistically significant. GFAP staining in the retina and ON tissues was highest in Group 1 and lowest in Group 4. ON thickness was greater in Group 2 than in Group 3, but the difference was also not statistically significant. CONCLUSıON: Although neither treatment demonstrated superiority over the other, both oral citicoline and idebenone provided neuroprotection in TON, as evidenced by improved electrophysiological function, greater retina ganglion cell survival, and elevated systemic antioxidant markers.

papers.title: Development of a conceptual model for fluid overload in children with nephrotic syndrome: a qualitative study of parent-reported observable experiences.
papers.abstract: Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is characterized by persistent or relapsing and remitting fluid overload. To identify the effectiveness of clinical treatments that target fluid overload among young children with NS, researchers seek to better understand the observable signs, events, or behaviors related to fluid overload among children too young to reliably self-report. This manuscript describes a conceptual model developed to inform an observer-reported outcome (ObsRO) appropriate for evaluating fluid overload in young children with NS. Semistructured interviews were conducted with caregivers of children aged 2-11 with NS via Zoom videoconferencing, telephone, or in-person. Eligible NS diagnoses were focal segmental glomerular sclerosis, minimal change disease, IgM nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, or childhood-onset NS not biopsied. Thematic content analysis was used to identify major themes in parent characterizations of their children's experience with fluid overload. Twenty-six caregivers of children with NS completed interviews. Interview content demonstrated that swelling had an impact on physical functioning (upper extremity function, activities of daily living, and mobility/walking), physical symptoms (appetite, fatigue, gastrointestinal distress, pain, and sleep), essential function (breathing, urination, and vision), behavior (crying and irritability), and social functioning (included daycare/school, family/friend relationships, and recreational activities). Domains will inform development of a clinical outcome assessment set for a validation study.

papers.title: Triphasic waves in leptomeningeal metastases and cycling alternating pattern of encephalopathy during sleep.
papers.abstract: Triphasic waves (TWs), now termed generalized periodic discharges with triphasic morphology, may be mistaken for nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), particularly in critically ill patients. Changes in vigilance over time can help distinguish encephalopathic patterns from ictal activity. A 69-year-old woman with breast cancer and leptomeningeal metastases developed progressive mutism and impaired consciousness. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed atypical cells and markedly elevated protein, while brain MRI demonstrated bilateral sulcal hyperintensities, most prominent in the posterior regions. An EEG performed 1 week after bevacizumab and paclitaxel were discontinued showed only mild background slowing without epileptiform discharges. A repeat EEG 1 week later showed nearly continuous TWs. The discharges disappeared during spontaneous sleep and recurred periodically, consistent with a cyclic alternating pattern of encephalopathy during sleep (CAPE). In the absence of significant metabolic and toxic derangements, these features favored an encephalopathic rather than ictal pattern. Given the advanced disease and poor prognosis, care remained supportive and palliative. This case highlights the importance of interpreting TWs within their clinical context and in relation to the state of vigilance. Their disappearance at sleep onset, with periodic recurrence during sleep producing a CAPE, supports an encephalopathic rather than ictal interpretation, helping to avoid misdiagnosis of NCSE and unnecessary administration of antiseizure medications.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

papers.title: Current findings, application, and diagnosis of magnetic resonance imaging in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder within the motor neuron disease (MND) spectrum, characterized by progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. The clinical phenotype ranges from pure motor syndromes to forms with cognitive and behavioral impairment, and the pathological burden extends beyond the motor system. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, supported by electrophysiology and exclusion of mimics. Therefore, objective imaging biomarkers are urgently needed. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used as an auxiliary and differential diagnostic tool in ALS. T1- and T2-weighted imaging can assess cortical thickness, gray matter atrophy, and signal changes. Diffusion tensor imaging probes white matter microstructure. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy detects neurochemical alterations. Resting-state functional MRI assesses functional connectivity and network organization. Susceptibility-weighted imaging is sensitive to iron and calcium deposition. Ultra-high-field MRI provides higher resolution and improved metabolite quantification. This critical review summarizes current findings on MRI in ALS, but importantly organizes the evidence by the specific question being addressed: pathological/histological correlates, diagnostic or discriminatory performance, and clinical associations with phenotype, severity, progression, and prognosis. We also discuss major limitations, including methodological heterogeneity, limited standardization, small and clinically heterogeneous cohorts, frequent use of healthy rather than disease controls, and scarce multicenter validation. Although advanced MRI has revealed robust group-level alterations, none of these techniques has yet become established in routine clinical diagnosis of ALS. We, therefore, distinguish promising research findings from validated clinical biomarkers and outline priorities for future translation.

papers.title: Weighted co-expression reveals early circadian and metabolic dysregulation in precystic kidneys.
papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) initiates long before cysts appear, yet the molecular triggers of this precystic phase remain poorly defined. To gain more insight into these early alterations, we applied cross-species Weighted Gene Coexpression Network Analysis (WGCNA) to renal transcriptomes from inducible Pkd1-knockout (iKsp-Pkd1del) mice across precystic and cystic stages. Instead of constructing a new network, expression profiles were projected onto three hundred and forty-seven curated rat kidney co-expression modules from the TXG-MAPr framework, enabling direct systems-level comparison with conserved injury signatures. Forty-two transcriptionally active modules emerged, including twenty-one already deregulated during the morphologically normal precystic phase. Early upregulated modules showed activation of circadian regulators (Bmal1/Arntl, Per1, Per3, Npas2) and sterol biosynthesis under Srebf2 control, whereas mitochondrial and oxidative-phosphorylation modules were markedly repressed. Transcription-factor enrichment revealed distinct regulatory axes: circadian control by BMAL1, metabolic regulation through SREBP2 (encoded by Srebf2), and inflammatory/cytokine signaling mediated by STAT3, p53, and NF-κB. These regulatory programs diverged transcriptionally within two weeks of Pkd1 loss, establishing an epithelial-driven phase characterized by circadian misalignment, metabolic rewiring, mitochondrial suppression and concomitant low-level inflammatory signaling. Inflammatory and stress-response modules intensified during later cystic stages. Notably, Pkd2 clustered within a small but transcriptionally active high-ranked module suggesting early perturbation of the polycystin complex. Together, these data define precystic ADPKD as a convergence of independent epithelial programs accompanied by early inflammatory engagement that precedes overt cyst expansion, providing a modular framework for early biomarker discovery and therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Study on methods for deriving spatial distribution of electron temperature and density from RGB (red-green-blue) digital image in non-thermal equilibrium plasma.
papers.abstract: A method used to derive the spatial distributions of electron temperature and density in non-thermal equilibrium plasma, respectively, from the relative and absolute intensities of RGB (red-green-blue) JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group) images acquired by using a digital camera is investigated. Since the RGB values of the JPEG image obtained from the complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor sensor of commercial digital cameras are automatically corrected, the RGB values are calibrated by simultaneously observing lamps with known RGB values using the camera and a spectrometer calibrated for absolute sensitivity as well as determining the correlation between the RGB values and emissivity. The validity of the calibrated RGB values is confirmed by observing the blackbody radiation of a candle flame using the camera and the spectrometer. In the case of optically thin plasmas, excitation radiation with a stronger intensity than bremsstrahlung radiation is observed. Since this strong excitation radiation is reflected in the RGB values, the electron temperature is derived from the relative RGB values by relating the excitation temperature obtained by using the line-pair method to the electron temperature obtained from continuum spectral analysis using bremsstrahlung radiation. The average grayscale calculated from the RGB values reflects the density distribution of the object's presence. The spatial distributions of electron temperature and density are obtained from the digital image using RGB relative values and the average grayscale, respectively.

papers.title: Sphenoidal Meningioma with Focal Seizures Masquerading as Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome in HIV Patient.
papers.abstract: Seizures in adults with HIV can result from structural lesions, opportunistic infections, immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) or medication effects, making accurate diagnosis challenging. We report a 47-year-old woman with HIV who developed recurrent focal-onset seizures evolving to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures beginning approximately 4 weeks after initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART). Neurological examination was unremarkable. Electroencephalography revealed focal slowing over the left anterior temporal region without generalised epileptiform discharges. Targeted infectious testing, including Toxoplasma gondii , Cryptococcus neoformans and Mycobacterium tuberculosis , was negative. Brain magnetic resonance imaging performed at the time of evaluation demonstrated a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass over the left sphenoid wing measuring 3.0 cm × 4.3 cm, isointense on T1-and T2-weighted sequences, with vasogenic oedema and midline shift, consistent with meningioma. Seizure control was achieved with antiseizure medication; however, definitive treatment required gross total surgical resection. Following surgery, the patient remained seizure-free at 12 months of follow-up. Although ART initiation initially suggested central nervous system IRIS, preserved immune function, negative infectious workup and characteristic imaging confirmed a structural aetiology. This case highlights the importance of a broad differential diagnosis and integrating clinical, electrophysiological, infectious and imaging data to identify treatable structural lesions in adults with HIV.

papers.title: Mapping Brain-Computer Interface Research in Depression (1995-2026): A Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as promising tools for neuromodulation and emotion regulation in depression. This study aimed to systematically map the global research landscape, thematic evolution, and emerging trends of BCI applications in depressive disorders through bibliometric analysis. Data were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and analyzed using the R package bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. Publication trends, country and institutional contributions, journal impact, author influence, and keyword-based clustering and burst analysis were comprehensively evaluated. A total of 239 publications authored by 1284 researchers from 239 institutions across 39 countries were identified. The United States and China had the highest publication outputs, while the United Kingdom showed high citation impact. Laureate Institute for Brain Research was the most productive institution and showed the strongest institutional collaboration, while NeuroImage: Clinical showed the highest journal h-index. Masaya Misaki was the leading author according to publication and citation indicators. Keyword analysis identified six major thematic clusters involving neurophysiological and cognitive features, EEG asymmetry and affective regulation, clinical neurofeedback, connectivity and self-regulation, fMRI-based emotion regulation, and psychiatric symptom/network correlates. "Emotion" showed the strongest keyword burst, while recent bursts in "real-time fMRI neurofeedback," "prefrontal cortex," and "emotion regulation" indicated increasing research attention to circuit-level regulation. The field has evolved from EEG-based characterization toward network-level and real-time neurofeedback research. These findings identify emerging research directions while highlighting the need for further methodological standardization and clinical validation.

papers.title: Clinical Validation of the New EEG Trend, Brain State of the Newborn, Against aEEG Interpretation.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown that the novel EEG trend, Brain State of the Newborn (BSN), is useful for monitoring recovery of electrocortical activity in high-risk newborns. Here, we validate the automatically computed BSN trend against visual amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) interpretation in asphyxiated hypothermia-treated infants. A total of 731 3-h aEEG epochs from 85 hypothermia-treated infants were randomized in order and scored independently by two clinical experts blinded for clinical data. First, we compared the BSN values to the aEEG scores at epoch level. Second, we assessed how the BSN trends align with aEEG scores in depicting electrocortical recovery. The BSN values showed robust differentiation between the experts' aEEG background scores (p ≤ 0.001 for all pairwise comparisons; effect size 1.0-6.5). Recovery of the BSN trend was also strongly correlated to the expert-defined aEEG recovery to continuous normal voltage (Spearman's ρ = 0.72, p < 0.001). The objective and fully automated BSN trend provides an effective, real-time complement to the visual aEEG interpretation. High BSN levels are reliable indicators of electrocortical recovery in hypothermia-treated infants. Future prospective studies are needed to establish evidence-based and context-sensitive clinical guidelines for the use of BSN in routine clinical care.

papers.title: Early and persistent blood pressure dysregulation in individuals with subacute motor incomplete spinal cord injury.
papers.abstract: Blood pressure (BP) dysregulation after spinal cord injury (SCI) may disrupt circadian BP rhythms, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and hypertension. These disturbances are independent predictors of cardiovascular disease, yet evidence in older adults with subacute motor incomplete SCI is limited. To characterize nocturnal dipping status, BP variability, and daytime and nighttime hypertension at admission to inpatient rehabilitation, and to assess changes during rehabilitation. Observational cohort study. Primary inpatient rehabilitation center. Individuals with motor incomplete SCI who completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring shortly after admission and before discharge. Not applicable. Nocturnal dipping (% reduction from nighttime to daytime systolic BP), BP variability, and hypertension defined using general population thresholds. Participants with motor incomplete SCI were included (n = 34, mean age 61 years, 82% male, 44% cervical injury). At admission, 82% were classified as non-dippers or reverse dippers. High BP variability was present in 59% for systolic BP and 29% for diastolic BP. Hypertension occurred in 21% during daytime and 59% during nighttime. All but one participant exhibited at least one BP-related risk factor. No changes were observed in dipping status, BP variability, and mean BP levels between admission and discharge (all p > 0.05). Marked BP dysregulation is evident early after motor incomplete SCI, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and nocturnal hypertension, despite daytime BP appearing within normal limits in most participants. These disturbances persisted throughout rehabilitation, indicating ongoing autonomic dysregulation that may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk.
papers.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine

papers.title: Transient Alerting Effects of Karolinska Sleepiness Scale Ratings on Physiological and Driving Performance Indicators.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine whether subjectively rating sleepiness on the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS) gives rise to an alerting effect and, if so, how long it persists. Data from five driving simulator studies involving 83 participants were pooled. Time-locked trajectories of blink duration, blink closing velocity, heart rate, electroencephalographic (EEG) parietal α and frontal θ power, and lateral lane position variability were analysed around each KSS rating using linear mixed-effects models with condition-specific KSS baselines, a transient post-rating component, a late post-rating offset, and time-on-task terms. Immediately after the rating, several indicators shifted in an alerting direction: blink duration and standard deviation of lateral position (SDLP) decreased, blink closing velocity and heart rate increased, and parietal α power generally decreased. Frontal θ showed a more condition-dependent response. The estimated duration of the transient component was indicator dependent, ranging from 40 s for heart rate to the upper bound of the 120-s analysis window for SDLP. These findings have practical implications for driver sleepiness detection system development, validation protocols, and type-approval processes that rely on KSS as a reference measure. If ratings themselves are associated with short-lived physiological or behavioural changes, the timing and modality of KSS administration become important for ensuring valid ground truth labels. Future studies with control conditions, randomized or jittered rating times, and real-road data are needed to determine whether the rating-associated changes are causal and generalisable.

papers.title: SERS of Bottled Water: Automated PET Nanoplastic Detection and Quantification.
papers.abstract: Nanoplastics represent an emerging contaminant of growing environmental and public health concern, with polyethylene terephthalate (PET) being on topic due to its dominant use in beverage packaging. This study presents a SERS approach for the detection and quantification of PET nanoplastics in commercial bottled water, combining SERS with colloidal silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) and commercial solid SERS substrates, with automated Pearson correlation spectral classification. Mapping SERS samples of PET-bottled water combined with a Python identification algorithm enabled the detection of PET nanoplastics, while SEM-EDX analysis confirmed the presence of nanoscale carbon-oxygen particles consistent with PET stoichiometry. Beyond PET, phthalocyanine pigment nanoparticles, likely originating from bottle package, and inorganic residues including calcite, gypsum, and sodium nitrate were simultaneously identified, demonstrating the multianalyte capability of the approach. Using colloidal AgNPs, the estimated PET nanoplastic concentration was 17.25 ± 1.6 million particles per 0.5 L bottle (34.5 ± 3.2 million particles/L), comparative with values reported by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) and stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy in comparable studies. The method requires minimal sample preparation, limited to concentration by evaporation, without digestion or extraction steps, and preliminary results can be obtained within a few hours. These findings establish SERS combined with automated spectral analysis as a practical and sensitive screening tool for nanoplastic monitoring in drinking water, reporting particle concentrations directly in the number of particles per liter and with potential applicability to broader water quality analysis.

papers.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
papers.abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury induces neuroplastic changes within the central nervous system (CNS) that may persist beyond reconstruction and rehabilitation. The purpose was to compare neurocognitive performance and cortical oscillatory activity between open-skill athletes (eg, soccer, basketball, or handball players) without ACL injury history and athletes with ACL reconstruction (ACLR) during a probabilistic go/no-go task. It was hypothesized that athletes with ACLR would exhibit poorer behavioral performance and less efficient oscillatory dynamics, particularly higher theta and lower suppression of beta and alpha power oscillations after goal stimulus onset. Controlled laboratory study. A total of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR) performed a probabilistic go/no-go task while electroencephalographic recording was performed. Time-frequency analysis targeted midfrontal theta (4-7 Hz), left-lateralized central beta (15-25 Hz), and posterior alpha (8-12 Hz) oscillations during prestimulus and target stimulus windows. Linear mixed-effects models examined group differences in cognitive performance and oscillatory power. Athletes with ACLR showed slower response times and lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09). Midfrontal theta power was attenuated for the ACLR group during the prestimulus phase (d = 0.60) yet elevated during target phase trials (d = 0.48), indicating a shift from proactive to reactive cognitive control in athletes with ACLR. Left-lateralized central beta (d = 0.61) and posterior alpha suppression (d = 0.55) were reduced, reflecting impaired motor cortical disinhibition and less efficient visual-attentional resource deployment, especially under high uncertainty conditions. Athletes with ACLR showed persistent alterations in the cortical oscillatory mechanisms associated with conflict monitoring, motor preparation, and attentional allocation under uncertainty. These neurocognitive alterations may compromise adaptive motor responses in sport contexts characterized by high uncertainty and cognitive mental demand, potentially increasing reinjury risk. These findings support the integration of neurocognitive assessment into return-to-sport protocols. Alterations in cortical oscillatory dynamics during decision-making under uncertainty may reflect reduced efficiency in cognitive control, motor preparation, and attentional allocation, which are not detected by standard assessments. Exercise professionals should consider integrating these assessments into return-to-sport protocols to address the persistent CNS alterations that may underlie reinjury risk in athletes with ACLR.
papers.journal: The American journal of sports medicine

papers.title: Neuropsychiatric Features of Individuals With LGI1-Antibody Encephalitis.
papers.abstract: Leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 antibody (LGI1-Ab) encephalitis is one of the most common forms of autoimmune encephalitis and is associated with prominent psychiatric features. Psychiatric phenotyping of this condition has relied on small studies and has lacked detail. In this retrospective study, the authors reviewed the psychiatric symptomatology and clinical course among patients with a confirmed diagnosis of LGI1-Ab encephalitis. The mean±SD age of the study sample (N=31) was 60.7±14.2 years; 71% of patients were men. The time to diagnosis was 4.9±5.8 months, and the follow-up time was 55.8±36.7 months. Eighteen patients had documented hyponatremia, and 22 were treated as inpatients. Psychiatric (71%), cognitive (81%), and neurological (84%) symptoms were present at similar rates, despite 97% of the patients coming from neurology referrals. Patients had a diverse range of seizures, including faciobrachial dystonic seizures. Of 19 patients undergoing detailed psychometric analysis, impairments were noted in memory or orientation (100%), executive function (63%), naming (47%), processing speed (37%), attention (32%), verbal fluency (26%), language (11%), and visuospatial abilities (11%). Patients had psychotic symptoms (42%), agitation or aggression (39%), emotional lability (35%), anxiety (26%), and subjective experiential phenomena (16%). Many patients had psychiatric sequelae that resolved after treatment, but a modest proportion of patients experienced ongoing apathy (6%), behavioral disinhibition (13%), obsessive-compulsive disorder (10%), subjective experiential phenomena (13%), and sleep disorders (29%). These findings show that cognitive impairment and psychopathology are frequent in LGI1-Ab encephalitis. Future research could examine neuroimaging, psychiatric symptoms, and cognitive deficits in further detail.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuropsychiatry and clinical neurosciences

papers.title: TCAP links environmental cues to circadian control of the cardiac sarcomere.
Neural circuits, cognition, and behavior in diffuse glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse gliomas arise within and become functionally integrated into neural circuits, establishing bidirectional interactions between malignant cells and the surrounding brain. Neuronal activity promotes glioma growth and progression, while glioma cells remodel the excitability, connectivity, and functional organization of the neural circuits they infiltrate. Pathological excitation-inhibition imbalance can impair cortical information processing, while tumor infiltration simultaneously disrupts, preserves, and induces adaptive reorganization of distributed functional networks. Language processing provides a well defined framework for examining these competing effects because language processing depends on distributed cortical and subcortical networks whose organization can be interrogated using neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and direct cortical stimulation. The pattern and severity of glioma-associated language dysfunction reflect the interaction among tumor location, growth kinetics, molecular and histopathological features, white matter involvement, and the capacity for adaptive redistribution of function within ipsilateral and contralateral networks. Slowly growing gliomas can permit substantial functional reorganization, whereas rapidly infiltrating tumors may constrain the time and biological substrate available for effective network adaptation. In this review, we examine reciprocal glioma-neural circuit interactions, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms of glioma-associated neuronal hyperexcitability and the disruption, preservation, and adaptive remodeling of language networks.

papers.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco.
papers.abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor-odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a 'trunk-branch' network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR-Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

papers.title: Pain in rare disorders.
papers.abstract: Rare disorders collectively affect more than 300 million people worldwide and often require lifelong multidisciplinary care. Although pain is not universal, it is a clinically important and frequently underrecognized manifestation in many rare disorders, contributing to impaired functioning, psychological distress, reduced participation and quality of life, and caregiver burden. Assessment and management are complicated by heterogeneous pain mechanisms, limited disease-specific evidence, fragmented care pathways, and a lack of standardized guidance. This Perspective proposes a clinically oriented framework for understanding and managing pain in rare disorders. Rather than reviewing individual diseases, it highlights the diversity and evolution of nociceptive, neuropathic, inflammatory, ischemic, nociplastic, and mixed pain mechanisms and the need for repeated, multidimensional, mechanism-informed assessment. Individualized management should integrate appropriate pharmacological and disease-modifying treatments with rehabilitation, psychological support, education, self-management, and multidisciplinary care. Digital health technologies may support longitudinal monitoring and access to specialist expertise, although their use requires appropriate validation and integration with clinical services. Literature was identified through searches in Oria, Oslo Metropolitan University's library discovery service, with no lower date restriction and including publications available up to June 2026.

papers.title: Occupational Therapy in LGBTQ + Affirming Primary Care: Referral, Intervention, and Outcomes.
papers.abstract: ImportanceLGBTQ + clients experience healthcare barriers that may shape daily routines, health management, and participation. Little is known about occupational therapy referral pathways and outcomes in LGBTQ + affirming primary care.ObjectiveTo describe referral characteristics, occupational performance concerns, intervention focus, and client-reported outcomes among LGBTQ + clients referred to occupational therapy.DesignRetrospective pilot program evaluation using clinical documentation and outcome data from July 2025 through March 2026, with a June 2026 analysis cutoff.SettingTwo Midwestern primary care settings where occupational therapy screening and referral processes were developed; ongoing intervention occurred through outpatient occupational therapy.ParticipantsThirty-nine referred clients were included in descriptive analyses; 38 received intervention beyond evaluation; 21 had complete baseline and follow-up Canadian Occupational Performance Measure data.InterventionIndividualized outpatient occupational therapy focused on client-identified concerns.Outcomes and MeasuresReferral and treatment characteristics, occupational performance concerns, coded occupational focus, and Canadian Occupational Performance Measure Performance and Satisfaction ratings.ResultsCommon concerns included instrumental activities of daily living (94.9%), health management/self-management (92.3%), activities of daily living (82.1%), and work or school participation (82.1%). The most common primary intervention focus was health management and chronic condition self-management (65.8%). Among participants with outcome data, COPM Performance scores improved by 2.29 points and Satisfaction scores improved by 2.58 points.Conclusions and RelevanceOccupational therapy may support LGBTQ + clients referred from primary care by addressing needs related to health management, routines, self-care, and participation through individualized outpatient intervention. Prospective multisite research is needed.
papers.journal: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association

papers.title: Clinical characteristics of paediatric-onset type 2 diabetes: a comparison by weight status in the Hong Kong childhood diabetes registry 2008 to 2023.
papers.abstract: Although obesity is a major risk factor for paediatric type 2 diabetes (T2DM), many Asian youths present without obesity. This phenotype remains under-recognised and poorly described. This study aimed to compare the clinical and metabolic characteristics of children newly diagnosed with T2DM, stratified by weight status, in Hong Kong. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using data from the Hong Kong Childhood Diabetes Registry (2008-2023). We compared the clinical and metabolic features of children with and without obesity who were newly diagnosed with T2DM. A total of 689 children (96 % Chinese) were included and 35 % were children without obesity. While age at diagnosis was similar between groups, children without obesity exhibited a higher prevalence of family history of T2DM (80.6 % vs. 67.5 %; p<0.0001), more frequent presentations of classical symptoms and diabetic ketoacidosis with or without hyperosmolar hyperglycaemia state (4.6 % vs. 1.6 %, p=0.0262), and higher HbA1c and blood glucose levels at diagnosis, with lower HOMA-%B, suggesting greater β-cell dysfunction. Conversely children with obesity had higher insulin resistance. They also had higher prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hypertension, hyperuricaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Insulin therapy was more frequently required at diagnosis in children without obesity (16.3 % vs. 8 %, p=0.001). These results highlight a distinct T2DM phenotype in Chinese children without obesity, marked by severe hyperglycaemia and a higher rate of insulin requirement at diagnosis. Increased clinical vigilance for this under-recognised group is warranted to optimise management at diagnosis, with long term outcomes to be address in future longitudinal studies.
papers.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

papers.title: Opposing modulation of QUAC1/ALMT12 by S-type channel inhibition and R-type channel activation during elevated-CO2 and ABA-induced stomatal movement.
papers.abstract: Atmospheric CO2 concentrations, now 50% higher than pre-industrial levels, induce plant stomatal closure. The slow (S)-type anion channels in guard cells are activated by elevated CO2/bicarbonate and promote that process. However, the response of the rapid (R)-type anion channels to CO2/bicarbonate remains unclear. Here, we show that bicarbonate fails to activate the R-type anion channel QUAC1 (ALMT12) in either Xenopus oocytes or guard cell protoplasts, which indicates that the two channel types are differentially in response to CO2/bicarbonate. Furthermore, we demonstrate that QUAC1/ALMT12 negatively regulates CO2/bicarbonate-induced stomatal closure, achieved through its inhibition of SLAC1. As such, ALMT12 has opposite functional consequences in ABA vs CO2 pathways due to differential upstream activation.

papers.title: Correction to "Bidirectional relations between subjective academic stress, sleep duration, and subjective well-being among Chinese adolescents: Evidence from a large-scale longitudinal study".
Performance of Children's Sleep Disturbance Scale for the Diagnosis of Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Children with Cleft Lip and Palate.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate associations between Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC) findings and polysomnographic parameters and the diagnostic performance of its Sleep Breathing Disorders (SBD) and Excessive Daytime Sleepiness (EDS) subscales for identifying obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in children with non-syndromic cleft conditions.DesignProspective, analytical, cross-sectional diagnostic study.SettingTertiary craniofacial referral center.Patients, ParticipantsChildren aged 3 years 8 months to 13 years with non-syndromic cleft lip and palate or isolated cleft palate. Forty-two underwent polysomnography; 38 had valid recordings and 37 had complete paired questionnaire and polysomnographic data.Main Outcome Measure(s)Associations between SDSC scores and polysomnographic parameters; sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and accuracy of the SBD and EDS subscales for identifying PSG-defined OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥1 event/h).ResultsOSA was identified in 27 of 38 participants (71.1%) with valid recordings and was predominantly mild. SDSC total and subscale scores were not significantly correlated with polysomnographic parameters. The SBD subscale had sensitivity of 38.5% and specificity of 72.7%; the EDS subscale had sensitivity of 23.1% and specificity of 54.5%.ConclusionsSDSC findings showed limited agreement with polysomnography, and the SBD and EDS subscales could not reliably identify or exclude OSA. The SDSC may complement clinical assessment by characterizing caregiver-reported symptoms, but polysomnography remains necessary for objective diagnosis and severity classification.
papers.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association

papers.title: CD36 Gates Nocturnal Hypertension via the Renal AMPK/HDAC5/PER1 Axis.
papers.abstract: Nocturnal hypertension is a strong predictor of cardio-cerebrovascular disease, yet its underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we identified CD36 as a key regulator of blood pressure (BP) rhythms and as a gatekeeper of nocturnal hypertension. Its deficiency disrupts circadian BP rhythms. We continuously monitored 48-hour BP using telemetry in CD36 global knockout mice and renal proximal tubule-specific CD36 knockout mice. We also collected serum samples and ambulatory BP monitoring data from patients with nocturnal hypertension to assess the relationship between CD36 expression and nocturnal hypertension. A comprehensive screening of various factors affecting BP and circadian rhythms was conducted to explore the molecular mechanisms. Our telemetry data revealed significantly elevated BP during the daytime (inactive period) in both CD36 global knockout and renal proximal tubule-specific knockout mice compared with their control counterparts. Furthermore, levels of platelet CD36 were negatively correlated with the severity of nocturnal hypertension in humans. Mechanistically, CD36 modulates BP rhythms through the AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase)/HDAC5 (histone deacetylase 5)/PER1 pathway: its deficiency activates phosphorylated AMPK, leading to the dissociation of the HDAC5-PER1 complex, enhancing PER1 nuclear accumulation, and desynchronizing the oscillations of intrarenal renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system genes and clock-controlled genes, ultimately disrupting BP rhythm. Our findings highlight CD36 as a critical integrator that links renal clocks to BP homeostasis, establishing it as a potential predictor and therapeutic target for nocturnal hypertension.

papers.title: BMAL1-Sleep interactions modulate quality of life in allergic rhinitis patients with circadian dysregulation.
papers.abstract: Circadian CLOCK genes regulate sleep and circadian rhythms. Allergic rhinitis (AR) is frequently associated with sleep disturbances that can substantially impair patient quality of life (QoL). However, the relationship between circadian CLOCK gene expression in AR and sleep-related outcomes or QoL has not been established. This study included 133 participants (100 patients with AR and 33 healthy controls). Participants completed the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (RQLQ), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Circadian CLOCK gene expression in peripheral blood leukocytes was measured using qRT-PCR. The Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare the two independent groups and categorical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test. Linear regression evaluated the associations between circadian CLOCK gene expression and the RQLQ or sleep parameters. Patients with AR demonstrated significantly poorer sleep quality, longer sleep latency, more frequent nocturnal awakenings, and a higher prevalence of evening-type chronotypes along with dysregulated circadian gene expression in peripheral leukocytes compared to controls. Specifically, CLOCK and PER1 were upregulated and BMAL1 and CRY1 were downregulated.
