papers.title: [Clinical evaluation of maxillomandibular advancement in the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.abstract: Objective:To analyze the treatment efficacy of maxillomandibular advancement（MMA） in obstructive sleep apnea（OSA）. Methods:Twenty-two patients with moderate to severe OSA admitted to Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital from June 2021 to September 2025 were enrolled. All patients exhibited CPAP intolerance or poor treatment response, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy revealed centripetal collapse of the velopharynx and lateral pharyngeal wall collapse. All patients underwent MMA. The body mass index（BMI）, epworth sleepiness scale（ESS） score, polysomnography（PSG） index, and clinical efficacy were collected preoperatively and at 6 months postoperatively. Results:At 6 months postoperatively, among the 22 patients, 3 patients achieved cure（13.64%）, 10 were markedly effective（45.45%）, 6 were effective（27.27%） and 3 were ineffective（13.64%）, yielding an overall clinical effective rate of 86.36%. Compared with preoperative values, postoperative AHI decreased, LSaO2 increased, and ESS score were reduced（P<0.05）; no significant difference was found in BMI between preoperative and postoperative measurements（P>0.05）. Conclusion:MMA can effectively increase the upper airway volume, reduce the frequency of apnea-hypopnea, and improve nocturnal hypoxemia and daytime sleepiness in patients with OSA. For patients with moderate to severe OSA who are intolerant to CPAP and present with concurrent palatopharyngeal and lateral pharyngeal collapse, MMA serves as an effective treatment option.

papers.title: [Evaluation of airway obstruction and surgical outcomes in OSA patients with small tonsils through drug-induced sleep endoscopy].
papers.abstract: Objective:To evaluate the upper airway obstruction patterns in obstructive sleep apnea（OSA） patients with tonsils of grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° using drug-induced sleep endoscopy（DISE）, and to analyze the outcomes of DISE-guided surgery. A retrospective analysis was conducted on OSA patients with grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° tonsil size treated between 2017 and 2020. Obstruction characteristics were recorded according to the VOTE classification based on DISE. The characteristics of upper airway obstruction were compared across subgroups stratified by OSA severity and tongue base position（grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° : low-grade tongue base collapse; grade Ⅲ°-Ⅳ°: high-grade tongue base collapse）. Patients who underwent DISE-guided surgery and completed follow-up were further enrolled to assess surgical efficacy and identify factors affecting postoperative outcomes. A total of 112 patients were included in the DISE analysis, including 30 patients with low-grade tongue base collapse and 82 with high-grade tongue base collapse. Retrovelar obstruction had the highest prevalence（66.7% to 84.1%） among all obstruction sites. The proportion of oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse increased with the severity of OSA. Forty-five patients completed surgery and follow-up. Surgery was performed according to DISE-based surgical planning. The surgical success rate in the low-grade tongue base collapse group（76.9%） was higher than that in the high-grade tongue base collapse group（52.9%）, but the difference was not statistically significant（P=0.259）. Postoperative AHI and percentage of time with oxygen saturation below 90% were significantly lower in the low-grade tongue base collapse group（P<0.05）. Among patients with complete concentric collapse of the retrovelar space（CCC） or complete oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse（O）, the surgical success rate was 81.8% in the low-grade tongue base collapse group versus 50.0% in the high-grade tongue base collapse group（P=0.193）. Among 6 high-grade tongue base collapse patients presenting with isolated CCC/O who underwent velopharyngeal surgery combined with partial glossectomy, 4 were effective（66.7%）; all 3 patients who underwent velopharyngeal surgery alone were ineffective. The velopharyngeal region is the primary site of obstruction in OSA patients with grade Ⅰ°-Ⅱ° tonsils and merits careful consideration during surgical planning. Patients with a low-grade tongue base collapse achieve better responses to DISE-guided surgery. For patients with high-grade tongue base collapse and CCC/O collapse subtype, combining tongue base surgery with velopharyngeal surgery may improve surgical outcomes.

papers.title: [Modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.abstract: Objective:To explore the feasibility, safety and efficacy of modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy in the treatment of specific types of obstructive sleep apnea（OSA）. Methods:The clinical data of 28 OSA patients with Friedman type Ⅱ or Ⅲ and mandibular micrognathia admitted to Foresea Life Insurance Guangzhou General Hospital and its collaborating institutions from January 2021 to December 2024 were collected and analyzed. All patients underwent modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy, and corresponding auxiliary procedures were combined according to the obstruction level: modified uvulopalatopharyngoplasty（UPPP） was added for patients with tonsillar hypertrophy or palatopharyngeal plane stenosis, lingual tonsillectomy for those with lingual tonsillar hypertrophy, and midline glossectomy or radiofrequency ablation of the tongue for those with significant tongue hypertrophy and retraction. Preoperative three-dimensional reconstruction of maxillofacial CT combined with Mimics software was performed for surgical planning to determine the parameters of double trapezoidal osteotomy（height: 14-16 mm, upper width: 20-22 mm, lower width: 23-25 mm）. During the operation, osteotomy, advancement（about 12 mm） and "Z"-shaped titanium plate fixation were completed according to the plan. Postoperative follow-up was conducted regularly to evaluate the efficacy. Results:All 28 operations were performed uneventfully, with an operation time of（95±15） minutes and intraoperative blood loss of（50±10） mL. Postoperatively, 6 patients had mild mental swelling and ecchymosis, which subsided spontaneously 3-5 days after surgery; 3 patients had transient numbness of the lower lip（in the distribution area of the mental nerve）, and the sensation recovered within 1 month after surgery; 2 patients had mandibular midline fracture and mild loosening of bone fragments due to forceful mouth opening and teeth clenching 3 days after surgery, which healed after fixation with dental arch guide plate for 3 months by the department of stomatology without affecting the final efficacy. All patients were hospitalized for 5-7 days after surgery and discharged uneventfully, without serious complications such as massive postoperative hemorrhage, dyspnea, surgical site infection, or titanium plate loosening. At the 6-month follow-up, the average snoring VAS scores before and after surgery were 7.75±1.82 and 3.61±1.75, respectively, and the average ESS scores were 9.93±4.97 and 5.54±3.09, respectively, with statistically significant differences（P<0.05）. Comparison of polysomnography results before and after surgery showed that the average AHI was（47.87±26.33） events/h and（20.89±18.35） events/h, respectively, with a statistically significant difference（P<0.01）, and the average AHI decreased by 56.36% after surgery compared with before surgery. The lowest oxygen saturation was（72.29±12.64）% before surgery and（83.50±7.93）% after surgery, with a statistically significant difference（P<0.01）. Facial evaluation at 6 months after surgery showed that the appearance of mandibular retrognathia was significantly improved in 26 patients（76.5%）. Conclusion:Modified genioglossus advancement with double trapezoidal osteotomy, fixed by tenon-and-mortise, yields high stability and a low complication profile. It can effectively enlarge the retroglossal airway, ameliorate obstructive sleep apnea（OSA） symptoms, optimize facial contour, and improve patient satisfaction simultaneously. This procedure holds high clinical application value for patients with Friedman type Ⅱ or Ⅲ（non-very severe） OSA associated with mandibular micrognathia. For patients with severe OSA, combined multi-level surgery or noninvasive ventilation therapy is required. Rigorous patient selection and exclusion of very severe cases are the keys to ensuring the success rate of treatment.

papers.title: [Clinical characteristics and surgical efficacy analysis of children with severe obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.abstract: Objective:To compare the clinical characteristics and sleep-related parameters of children with severe obstructive sleep apnea（OSA） exhibiting different surgical outcomes, and to identify risk factors associated with surgical efficacy. Methods:Children with severe OSA who underwent adenotonsillectomy in the Department of Otorhinolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery at Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital between July 2017 and July 2024 were enrolled. According to whether they achieved complete remission of OSA after surgery, children with severe OSA were classified into a cure group and a residual OSA group. Clinical characteristics and polysomnographic parameters were compared between the two groups, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors affecting postoperative outcomes. Results:A total of 99 children with severe OSA were included, 43（43.4%） achieved cure after surgery, and 56（56.6%） had residual OSA. Children in the residual OSA group had significantly higher preoperative age, body weight, body mass index（BMI）, and obstructive apnea-hypopnea index（OAHI） than those in the cure group（P<0.05）. In both groups, postoperative OAHI decreased significantly and the lowest nocturnal oxygen saturation（SpO2） increased significantly compared with preoperative values（P<0.05）. The proportions of sleep stages before and after surgery did not differ significantly between the two groups（P>0.05）. Receiver operating characteristic（ROC） analysis showed that preoperative OAHI predicted complete postoperative remission with an area under the curve of 0.65, when 24 events/h was used as the cutoff, the sensitivity was 42.9% and the specificity was 86.1%. Multivariable logistic regression indicated that older age and preoperative OAHI>24 events/h were independent risk factors for residual OSA after surgery. Conclusion:Although surgical treatment significantly improves respiratory events and hypoxemia in children with severe OSA, the incidence of residual OSA remains high. Older age and preoperative OAHI>24 events/h are important risk factors for postoperative residual OSA.

papers.title: [The influence of different reference planes on upper airway CT measurement in OSA patients].
papers.abstract: Objective:Upper airway CT has become a routine tool for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome（OSA） and for localizing the site of obstruction. However, the measurement protocols differ markedly among studies, especially in the choice of reference planes, which compromises data comparability and hampers the development of clinical guidelines and multicenter studies. By comparing CT measurements obtained with different reference planes, this study analyzes their discrepancies and applicable scopes, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for the standardization of precision diagnosis and multicenter research in OSA. Methods:All participants underwent polysomnography（PSG） and upper airway CT within two months. Key osseous and soft-tissue landmarks were identified, and the airway was reconstructed using four different reference planes: ①the native image plane; ②the Frankfort horizontal plane to posterior nasal spine（FH-PNS）; ③the plane defined by the anterior commissure, anterior nasal spine, and basion（V-ANS-Ba）; ④the plane defined by the posterior nasal spine and uvular tip（PNS-U）. Measurements included the soft-palate angle（ANS-PNS-U）, the tongue angle（GN-H-Me）, the hyoid-to-mandibular-plane distance（H-MP）, and the lengths of various airway segments. Results:from the four planes were compared. Results:This study enrolled 30 participants, including 15 patients with OSA whose median apnea-hypopnea index（AHI） was 31.6（18.5, 37.8） events/h and body mass index（BMI） was（26.8±9.0） kg/m², and 15 control subjects whose median AHI was 1.8（0.7, 2.5） events/h and BMI was（25.1±4.8） kg/m². The soft-palate angle, tongue angle, and hyoid-to-mandibular-plane distance showed excellent agreement across the four reference planes, with no significant differences（P>0.05）, indicating that plane selection does not affect measurements of inter-landmark distances and angles. In contrast, airway-segment lengths varied with the reference plane. In the FH-PNS system, lengths of SB-ET, SB-H, PNS-ET, and PNS-V were significantly greater than in the native images（P<0.05） and showed stronger correlations with AHI. In the V-ANS-Ba system, SB-H, PNS-H, and U-ET lengths increased significantly（P<0.05） and correlated better with AHI than those obtained using the FH-PNS system. Lengths measured using the PNS-U system showed no significant differences compared with native images（P>0.05）. Conclusion:①The choice of reference plane does not influence the measurement of distances and angles between key landmarks. ②The FH-PNS plane is well suited for analyses in the high head-and-neck region, the V-ANS-Ba plane offers a new perspective for comprehensive airway functional assessment, and the PNS-U plane introduces minimal distortion, yielding results closest to the native image.

papers.title: [Effects of perioperative non-invasive ventilation on patients undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery].
papers.abstract: Objective:To evaluate the efficacy and safety of perioperative noninvasive ventilation（NIV） in patients with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea（OSA） undergoing bariatric and metabolic surgery（MBS）. Methods:This retrospective study enrolled 135 obese patients who underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy or laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between January and December 2024. Patients were assigned to the NIV group（n=61） or control group（n=74） based on perioperative OSA severity and intervention strategy. Baseline characteristics and polysomnography parameters were compared. Perioperative surgical outcomes, short-term postoperative complications, and changes in arterial blood gas and blood pressure（preoperatively or before NIV vs postoperatively） were analyzed. Results:There were no significant differences between groups in age, sex, or surgical procedure（all P>0.05）. Body mass index（P=0.002）, waist circumference（P=0.040）, hip circumference（P=0.033）, preoperative apnea-hypopnea index（P<0.001）, and oxygen desaturation index（P<0.001） were significantly higher in the NIV group, whereas mean and lowest oxygen saturation were significantly lower（both P<0.001）. Operative time, intraoperative blood loss, and postoperative length of stay did not differ significantly between groups（all P>0.05）; however, the duration of endotracheal intubation was significantly longer in the NIV group（P<0.001）. Under a strict postoperative airway management protocol, despite prolonged intubation in the NIV group, the incidence of short-term postoperative complications did not differ significantly between groups（all P>0.05）. Compared with values before NIV, the NIV group showed increased pH（P<0.001）, decreased PaCO2 and blood lactate（P=0.001 and P<0.001, respectively）, and improved PaO2（P<0.001） as well as systolic（P=0.011） and diastolic blood pressure（P<0.001） after surgery, whereas no significant perioperative changes were observed in the control group. Significant between-group differences were present at baseline（before NIV vs preoperatively in controls; all P<0.05）, while postoperative physiological parameters were comparable between groups（all P>0.05）. Conclusion:In MBS patients with moderate-to-severe OSA, prophylactic perioperative NIV combined with postoperative airway management appears to be a safe and feasible strategy and may effectively improve early postoperative physiological status.

papers.title: [Expert consensus on multidisciplinary sequential diagnosis and treatment of sleep-disordered breathing in children].
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing（SDB） has a relatively high prevalence in children, and its pathogenesis is complex, involving interdisciplinary issues. Among its subtypes, obstructive sleep apnea （OSA） is the most common, accounting for approximately 90% of cases. Untreated SDB can impair growth and development, cognitive function, and cardiovascular health in affected children. At present, its diagnosis and treatment remain constrained by inadequate multidisciplinary collaboration, single-dimensional assessment, fragmented care, and the lack of a sequential care concept. This consensus was jointly developed by a multidisciplinary panel of experts in otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, orthodontics and stomatology, pediatrics, endocrinology, and psychiatry and psychology. In accordance with the principles of relevant guidelines issued by the World Health Organization （WHO） and the Chinese Medical Association, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation （GRADE） system was adopted to assess the quality of evidence and grade the strength of recommendations. Recommendations were formulated covering diagnostic assessment, multidisciplinary collaboration, sequential treatment, management of special populations, follow-up and health education, and future research directions, and a child-centered, stage-based, and dynamically adjusted multidisciplinary framework for sequential diagnosis and treatment was established, with the aim of standardizing clinical practice, enhancing comprehensive management, and improving the quality of life and long-term prognosis of affected children.

papers.title: [Research progress on the application of orofacial myofunctional therapy in adult obstructive sleep apnea syndrome].
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome（OSAHS） is a prevalent sleep disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse during sleep, which causes apnea and hypopnea. Although continuous positive airway pressure（CPAP） serves as the standard treatment, poor patient compliance drives the exploration of alternative and adjuvant therapies. Orofacial myofunctional therapy（OMT）, a non-invasive and low-cost therapeutic approach, improves OSAHS by strengthening upper airway muscle function. This paper systematically reviews domestic and international research advances of OMT in adult OSAHS treatment, summarizes its theoretical basis, therapeutic mechanisms, clinical efficacy, implementation protocols and influencing factors, and proposes prospects for future research based on existing limitations.

papers.title: [Clinical application of precise uvulopalatopharyngoplasty using minimally invasive anatomical needles].
papers.abstract: Objective:To investigate the clinical application safety and efficacy of minimally invasive anatomical needle-guided precise uvulopalatopharyngoplasty. Methods:The data of patients who underwent precise uvulopalatopharyngoplasty using minimally invasive anatomical needles in Department of Otolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery,the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University from March 2025 to March 2026 were retrospectively collected. The operation time, intraoperative usage, postoperative recovery, and postoperative complications were analyzed to explore the safety and effect of clinical application of this method. Results:A total of 22 cases of patients undergoing precise palatopharyngoplasty using minimally invasive anatomical needles were collected. All 22 patients simultaneously underwent total or partial tonsillectomy and palatopharyngoplasty, along with concurrent nasal cavity expansion surgery. The operation time for tonsillectomy-UPPP ranged from 15 to 25 minutes, with smooth surgical processes. No patients experienced complications such as respiratory difficulties or bleeding during hospitalization. All patients underwent pain scale assessment on the morning of the second day after surgery, with scores ranging from 1 to 3, an average score of 2.13. All patients were discharged 2-3 days after surgery. The patients were followed up for 4 weeks. One patient experienced slight pharyngeal bleeding 7 days after surgery. No patients were readmitted for treatment due to surgical area bleeding, and the surgical area had mostly returned to normal at the 4-week postoperative follow-up. Conclusion:Precise palatopharyngoplasty using minimally invasive anatomical needles has good surgical safety, minimal surgical trauma, lower postoperative pain levels, minimal soft tissue edema in the surgical area, and shortened postoperative hospital stay, making it worthy of clinical promotion.

papers.title: Sleep Efficiency and Physical Capacity in Adults With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Sleep efficiency and physical capacity are important factors in metabolic health among adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and may be influenced by common pathophysiological mechanisms. This study evaluated the association between physical capacity and objectively measured sleep efficiency in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. In this cross-sectional study, 136 adults were enrolled. Physical capacity was assessed using the Global Physical Capacity Score, hepatic steatosis was quantified using FibroScan, and sleep efficiency was assessed using wrist actigraphy. Linear and logistic regression analyses were performed after adjustment for potential confounding factors. Overall, 61.8% of participants had impaired sleep efficiency (< 85%). In the fully adjusted logistic regression model, participants with a Global Physical Capacity Score ≥ 6 had significantly lower odds of impaired sleep efficiency (odds ratio 0.42, 95% confidence interval 0.19-0.95; p = 0.037); when physical capacity was analysed as a continuous variable, the association was in the same direction but not statistically significant (odds ratio per 1-point increase 0.79, 95% confidence interval 0.61-1.03; p = 0.077). Stratified analyses showed a significant association among women (odds ratio 0.26, 95% confidence interval 0.07-0.92; p = 0.037; continuous model: odds ratio per 1-point increase 0.74, 95% confidence interval 0.51-1.06; p = 0.095), whereas no significant association was observed among men. Higher multidimensional physical capacity was associated with better objectively measured sleep efficiency. Assessment of physical capacity may therefore provide additional information when evaluating sleep-related risk in this population.

papers.title: How Circadian Rhythms Shape Emotional Reactivity and Regulation: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms exert a profound influence on human physiology and behaviour, providing temporal organisation to sleep-wake patterns, cognitive performance, and affective functioning. Increasing evidence indicates that misalignment between internal biological clocks and external environmental or social demands critically affects emotional health. This narrative review focuses on the role of circadian rhythms in shaping emotional reactivity and regulation, with particular attention to chronotype, social jet lag (SJL) and shift work. Evening chronotypes show greater vulnerability to negative affect, difficulties in emotion regulation and a higher incidence of psychiatric symptoms compared to morning types, who typically display greater emotional stability. SJL, prevalent during adolescence, has been associated with mood disturbances, anxiety and impaired regulatory capacities, with screen exposure and late-night activities acting as aggravating factors. Similarly, shift workers frequently experience circadian desynchronisation, which disrupts executive functions essential for adaptive emotion regulation and predisposes them to stress, irritability and long-term mental health problems. Although these findings underline the strong relationship between circadian misalignment and emotional dysfunction, inconsistencies in results highlight the need for methodological refinement. Future studies should combine subjective reports with physiological markers and adopt longitudinal designs to track long-term trajectories; controlled light exposure, structured sleep-wake routines and organisational policies for shift scheduling, may represent promising avenues to strengthen resilience. By elucidating the mechanisms through which circadian rhythms modulate emotions, research can contribute to improving prevention and treatment strategies for mood and anxiety disorders, ultimately enhancing psychological well-being.

Uncovering hidden structural and mechanical contrast via spectral photoacoustic imaging.
papers.abstract: Characterizing the mechanical and structural properties of materials is crucial for applications ranging from biomedicine to industrial non-destructive testing. While conventional photoacoustic imaging discards acoustic spectra or restricts spectral analysis to isolated microscopic resonances, we introduce Spectral Photoacoustic Imaging (SPAI) to analyze spatial-frequency information for revealing the mechanical and structural contrasts of macroscopic targets. In our proof-of-concept experiments, we demonstrate that SPAI can reveal contrast from subtle composition differences in commercially graded pencil leads where optical absorption yields negligible difference, extract the structural resonances of sub-surface cavities embedded in opaque 3D-printed blocks, and detect deeply buried internal voids through acoustic mode pattern perturbations. By combining broadband acoustic spectra with frequency-resolved modal patterns, this approach provides a practical framework for noninvasively probing structural and material signatures in complex targets.

papers.title: Symptom-level associations among sleep quality, depression, and social rhythm in people living with HIV: a network analysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance, depression, and social rhythm irregularity commonly co-occur in people living with HIV (PLWH), yet their symptom-level associations remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the network structure linking sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and social rhythm in PLWH and to identify central and bridge symptoms within this system. A cross-sectional sample of 737 people living with HIV (PLWH) in Changsha, China, was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Self-Rating Depression Scale, and Brief Social Rhythm Scale. A 32-node Gaussian graphical model was estimated using EBICglasso, with correlation types selected according to variable measurement levels. Expected influence (EI) and bridge expected influence (BEI) identified central and bridge symptoms, respectively, and were z-standardized for presentation. Community-size-normalized BEI was calculated to account for unequal community sizes, and its agreement with raw BEI rankings was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Node predictability was estimated using a separate Gaussian model, with the regularization parameter selected by 10-fold cross-validation. Edge-weight accuracy and centrality stability were evaluated using nonparametric and case-dropping bootstraps, respectively. Goldbricker screening and reduced-network sensitivity analysis assessed node redundancy and the robustness of centrality findings. The network consisted of 32 nodes and 174 nonzero edges, indicating substantial interconnections among sleep quality, depression, and social rhythm. Subjective sleep quality had the highest z-standardized expected influence (EI = 2.40) and bridge expected influence (BEI = 2.87). After community-size normalization, depressive sleep disturbance had the highest community-size-normalized bridge expected influence (nBEI = 0.045). Subjective sleep quality, daytime dysfunction, depressive sleep disturbance, and fatigue consistently comprised the four leading bridge nodes in both the bridge expected influence and community-size-normalized bridge expected influence analyses, although their ordering differed. Sleep quality, depression, and social rhythm were closely interconnected at the symptom level among PLWH. Subjective sleep quality, daytime dysfunction, depressive sleep disturbance, and fatigue may warrant prioritization in clinical assessment. Longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to determine whether targeting these symptoms can improve other symptoms across the network.

papers.title: Preclinical efficacy of extracellular vesicle therapy in peripheral nerve injury: a comprehensive systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) result in significant motor and sensory deficits, with autologous nerve grafting as the gold standard but limited by donor morbidity and incomplete recovery. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising cell-free therapy, offering potent paracrine signaling, safety, and immunological compatibility. This study systematically evaluated the preclinical efficacy of EV-based therapies for PNI. A systematic review and network meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to July 1, 2025. Eligible in vivo studies investigated EVs from any cell source in animal PNI models, compared with controls, and reported functional, structural, electrophysiological, or sensory outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the CAMARADES checklist. Three hierarchical meta-analyses compared EVs, structural grafts, cellular therapies, and combination strategies. The primary endpoint was sciatic functional index (SFI), and secondary outcomes included muscle preservation, sensory recovery, and electrophysiology. Thirty-five studies met inclusion, with 32 included in quantitative synthesis. EV therapy significantly improved SFI versus control (MD: 21.80; 95% CI 7.20-36.39; p = 0.0034), with greater effects in crush injuries and when combined with scaffolds, conduits, or autografts (up to MD: 54.41). Secondary outcomes showed improved gastrocnemius weight, muscle fiber area, nerve conduction velocity, and mechanical withdrawal thresholds. MSC-derived EVs, particularly scaffold-delivered, yielded the most consistent gains, while Schwann cell-derived EVs were effective as monotherapy. Mechanistically, EVs enhanced axonal growth, remyelination, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization while reducing inflammation. EV-based therapies significantly enhance functional, structural, and electrophysiological recovery in preclinical PNI models, with synergistic benefits when combined with structural supports. Standardization of EV production and delivery, and validation in clinically relevant models, are essential for translation into human therapy.

papers.title: Daily television viewing and social communication in preschool children: cross-sectional associations with outdoor activity.
papers.abstract: Daily television viewing may be associated with social-communication difficulties in early childhood, but whether this association is related to concurrent health-related behaviors remains unclear. This population-based cross-sectional study included 12,584 children aged 36-60 months from 96 kindergartens in Shanghai, China. Daily television viewing was parent-reported and categorized as ≤ 1 h/day or > 1 h/day. Social communication outcomes were assessed using the Social Communication Questionnaire (SCQ). Multivariable regression models estimated associations between daily television viewing and SCQ outcomes. Outdoor activity frequency, sleep duration, and BMI z-score were examined in exploratory cross-sectional indirect-association models. FDR correction was applied. Overall, 56.6% of children had daily television viewing > 1 h/day. Television viewing > 1 h/day was associated with a slightly higher SCQ total score (B = 0.185, 95% CI 0.054-0.316), social interaction domain (B = 0.107, 95% CI 0.029-0.186), and communication domain (B = 0.034, 95% CI 0.005-0.063). After additional adjustment for outdoor activity, sleep, and BMI z-score, these associations were attenuated and were no longer statistically significant. Outdoor activity frequency showed the largest exploratory indirect association, whereas indirect associations through sleep were smaller and those through BMI z-score were weak or inconsistent. Daily television viewing > 1 h/day was associated with slightly higher SCQ scores in preschoolers, but not with SCQ-positive status. This pattern suggests that TV viewing-related social communication difficulties should not be directly equated with ASD, but may represent a modifiable behavioral concern, highlighting outdoor activity as a potential focus for future interventions.

papers.title: Early sleep and sensory over-responsivity relate to insular functional connectivity with sensorimotor cortices and cerebellum in infants at varying likelihood for autism.
papers.abstract: Sleep problems and sensory over-responsivity (SOR) are common, co-occurring, and early emerging features of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Yet, the early neural mechanisms underlying these symptoms remain unclear. Here, we used resting-state fMRI data from the Infant Brain Imaging Study (IBIS) to examine how functional brain connectivity at 6 months may relate to parent-reported measures of sleep-onset problems and SOR in infants at varying familial likelihood for ASD. The right anterior insula (rAI) - a key hub of the salience network - was used in ROI-ROI analyses to investigate functional connectivity to cortical and cerebellar regions previously implicated in sleep disruption, sensory processing challenges, and ASD. Infants at high (HL) and low (LL) likelihood for ASD displayed divergent patterns of rAI connectivity with sensorimotor cortex, as well as cerebellar regions involved in sensorimotor processing and higher-order functions. Furthermore, stronger rAI connectivity with sensorimotor cortices and cerebellar regions was associated with worse sleep-onset problems and SOR in HL infants. In contrast, stronger rAI-cerebellar connectivity was related to fewer sleep-onset problems and SOR in LL infants. Our findings indicate that altered rAI connectivity may result in over-attribution of attention to sensory stimuli and highlight aberrant sensory prediction learning, which may underlie worse sleep problems and higher SOR in HL infants.

papers.title: Device-derived sleep metrics and nocturnal heart rate variability for discriminating bipolar from unipolar depressive episodes in adolescents: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing bipolar depression (BD) from unipolar depression (UD) in adolescents is clinically challenging because depressive symptoms overlap and reliable objective markers are lacking. Sleep and heart rate variability (HRV) have been implicated in mood disorders, but their value for differentiating adolescent BD from UD remains insufficiently studied. This study compared clinical characteristics, device-derived sleep metrics, and nocturnal HRV indices between adolescents with BD and UD, and explored whether physiological measures provided additional information associated with BD classification. In this single-center retrospective cross-sectional study, 110 inpatients aged 11-17 years with a current depressive episode were included, comprising 46 patients with BD and 64 with UD. Overnight portable sleep monitoring was performed during early inpatient assessment. Clinical characteristics, device-derived sleep parameters, and nocturnal HRV indices were extracted from medical records and device-generated reports. Between-group comparisons were corrected for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate. Hierarchical logistic regression models were used to examine the relative contribution of clinical variables, sleep metrics, and HRV indices. An exploratory parsimonious model was internally evaluated using repeated cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. Compared with the UD group, the BD group had a longer illness duration (24.0 [12.0, 48.0] vs. 12.0 [6.0, 26.0] months, q = 0.042) and a higher prevalence of self-harm history (93.5% vs. 68.8%, q = 0.031). No selected single-night device-derived sleep metric differed significantly between groups after false discovery rate correction. In contrast, several nocturnal HRV indices, including time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear measures, were significantly lower in the BD group. In the full hierarchical model incorporating clinical, sleep, and HRV variables, lower log-transformed total HRV power was the only physiological measure independently associated with BD classification (odds ratio per 1-standard-deviation increase = 0.34, 95% confidence interval: 0.16-0.69, p = 0.003). An exploratory parsimonious model including illness duration, self-harm history, and log-transformed total HRV power yielded an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.820 and an optimism-corrected value of 0.807. Adolescents with BD showed reduced device-derived nocturnal HRV compared with those with UD, particularly lower total HRV power, whereas the selected single-night portable sleep metrics showed limited discriminative value in this dataset. Reduced nocturnal HRV may represent an auxiliary objectively measurable physiological correlate for future research on the differential assessment of adolescent depressive episodes. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic assessment, repeated or longitudinal physiological monitoring, and external validation are needed before clinical application.

papers.title: Anorexia nervosa or pediatric acute-onset neuropsychiatric syndrome? A case report.
papers.abstract: Pediatric Acute-Onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome (PANS) is a rare heterogeneous condition characterized by rapid onset obsessions/compulsions and/or food restriction with at least two accompanying acute-onset neuropsychiatric symptoms. PANS is currently considered an exclusionary diagnosis with considerable overlap with psychiatric disorders including obsessive compulsive disorder, tics, and eating disorders. Little is known about the crossover between eating disorders and PANS, and there is minimal guidance on diagnostic and treatment considerations for these patients. This case report describes a 9-year-old female who presented for an initial assessment to a specialty outpatient eating disorder treatment center due to restrictive eating, fear of weight gain, body image disturbance, and obsessive-compulsive compensatory behaviors. She met diagnostic criteria for other specified feeding and eating disorder (OSFED)/atypical nervosa (AAN) and received family-based treatment (FBT) to target food restriction through parent-led refeeding. Despite weight stabilization and nutritional improvement in FBT, the patient experienced severe progressive functional deterioration. The patient was subsequently evaluated by an immune behavioral health (IBH) clinic and diagnosed with PANS. Treatment included gradual transition in care from the eating disorder clinic for AAN to IBH and sleep clinics for management of remaining neuropsychiatric symptoms. This report highlights a unique case of a patient with PANS features and body image/weight-driven food refusal. This case has potential implications for how eating disorder specialty providers asses for possible overlapping PANS. Criteria prompting consideration for PANS may include a combination of acute-onset restrictive eating, prepubertal body image disturbance, and progressive functional impairment and/or developmental regression despite weight restoration. This case also highlights implications of care coordination and triage across specialty clinics.

papers.title: Music and movement intervention for brain-heart disease in children with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1): a convergent mixed-methods feasibility study protocol.
papers.abstract: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a rare autosomal dominant inherited multi-systemic disease affecting neuromuscular, cognitive, and cardiac function. Congenital DM1 (CDM) is the most severe form of the disease and is associated with learning difficulties, autism-like traits, and cardiac conduction defects. There is no approved pharmacological therapy for CDM. While music interventions have been shown to positively impact children with similar brain and heart symptoms, like cerebral palsy and autism, this type of non-pharmacological intervention has not been tested in CDM. Therefore, this convergent mixed-methods study will assess the tolerability and feasibility of a 10-week music and movement intervention for children with CDM. Participants will be recruited from the pediatric neuromuscular clinic at the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO). In a dyad participation model, parents of participants will also engage to inform the overall feasibility. There will be two groups with 6-8 participants each. Group allocation will not be randomized but will be based on age and physical and mental ability. A baseline visit will be followed by a 10-week intervention phase with one music and movement intervention session per week. Sessions will include physical assessments and questionnaires. The primary outcome is the feasibility and tolerability of these music interventions. Secondary outcome measures include cognitive and physical assessments, as well as measures of quality of life, sleep quality, and biomarkers. This study will demonstrate the feasibility and tolerability of music and movement intervention for pediatric participants with CDM, while providing an indication of its impacts on brain and heart function for this multi-system disease. Results from this study will inform the implementation of a larger-scale trial as well as the development of other non-pharmacological feasibility studies in this population. Clinicaltrials.gov number: NCT06809049. Registered 30 Jan 2025. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06809049?id=NCT06809049&rank=1 .

papers.title: Development and evaluation of a prevention and health promotion literacy questionnaire for schoolchildren in France.
papers.abstract: Developing health literacy, especially for school-aged children, is essential to preventing the adoption of unhealthy behaviours. Specific measurement tools can help assess needs and evaluate actions within an evidence-based approach. This study aimed to develop a questionnaire to assess health literacy, with a focus on prevention and health promotion, and to evaluate its psychometric properties among French schoolchildren aged 8-11. We developed a prevention and health promotion literacy questionnaire following three steps: (i) item selection from eight prevention and health promotion domains (attitudes towards health, nutrition, physical activity, addictions, sun exposure, sleep, screen use, and safety), each organized into four parts according to the dimensions of the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, Behaviour (COM-B) model, and content validity, (ii) pre-testing and refinement of the questionnaire, and (iii) assessment of psychometric properties and item reduction after administration to a sample of children in 30 schools. A total of 699 children completed the questionnaire (mean age 9.6 ± 0.5 years; 51.1% girls). Dimensional analysis yielded a 29-item questionnaire with a three-factor structure: health-related motivation (dim. 1), screen use behaviours (dim. 2), and multi-thematic health knowledge dimension (dim. 3). The questionnaire demonstrated good acceptability and satisfactory reliability (Cronbach's alpha = 0.77 for the overall questionnaire, 0.75 for dim. 1, 0.71 for dim. 2, and 0.55 for dim. 3). The questionnaire developed in this study enables an assessment of health literacy from a prevention and health promotion perspective in French school children. It offers a practical resource to identify needs and guide health promotion actions in schools.

papers.title: Examining the distinctiveness of the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire from depressive symptoms in patients with heart failure.
papers.abstract: The Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ) is widely used to assess health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in patients with heart failure (HF), but conceptual overlap with depressive symptoms may complicate interpretation of patient-reported outcomes. To evaluate the discriminant validity of the MLHFQ relative to the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and examine the independent association between depressive symptoms and HRQOL. This secondary cross-sectional analysis included 306 patients with cardiologist-confirmed HF in Jordan. Exploratory factor analysis examined the underlying structure of the combined MLHFQ and PHQ-9 items, and hierarchical regression analyses evaluated the association between depressive symptoms and HRQOL after adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Five correlated factors emerged from the combined MLHFQ and PHQ-9 analysis, representing physical HRQOL, emotional HRQOL, treatment burden, Somatic Depressive Symptoms, and social role limitations. Partial conceptual overlap was observed primarily for fatigue, sleep disturbance, and selected emotional items, whereas most HF-specific items loaded on distinct HRQOL factors. Item-level correlations between the MLHFQ and PHQ-9 ranged from weak to moderate (r = .01-0.61). After adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, depressive symptoms explained an additional 25% of the variance in overall HRQOL, 18% in physical HRQOL, and 31% in emotional HRQOL. In a revised physical HRQOL model excluding overlapping items, depressive symptoms remained independently associated with poorer physical HRQOL, explaining an additional 13% of the variance. Depressive symptoms were strongly associated with perceived HRQOL, particularly within the emotional domain, while the MLHFQ captures broader HF-specific aspects of quality of life that remain distinguishable from depression. These findings support the discriminant validity and clinical usefulness of the MLHFQ while highlighting the importance of concurrent assessment of depressive symptoms when evaluating patient-reported outcomes in HF. papers.title: Effects of synbiotic supplementation on clinical symptoms and metabolic outcomes in patients with painful diabetic neuropathy: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN) is a relatively common complication of diabetes. Experimental studies have shown that dysbiosis can act as a key factor in neural hypersensitivity and pain perception. We aim to assess the effect of synbiotics on PDN. In a randomized, double-blind clinical trial, 60 patients with painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN) were assigned to receive either a synbiotic (a 109 CFU blend of Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, and Streptococcus strains and 74 mg of fructooligosaccharides) or a placebo for eight weeks. Compared to placebo, synbiotic significantly decreased the numerical rating score for pain (synbiotic: from 7.60 ± 0.85 to 3.20 ± 1.80; placebo: from 7.83 ± 0.95 to 6.43 ± 1.85; P < 0.001), reduced sleep interference (synbiotic: from 6.83 ± 1.46 to 2.60 ± 1.69; placebo: from 6.83 ± 1.46 to 5.33 ± 2.64; P < 0.001), and enhanced six out of eight domains of the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey questionnaire. Analysis of pain types in the short-form McGill Pain Questionnaire-2 showed significant improvements in hot-burning pain (P = 0.032), cold-freezing pain (P = 0.018), and tingling (P < 0.001), whereas numbness and other investigated pain types did not show significant changes during the intervention period. Furthermore, body mass index, fasting blood insulin and glucose levels, and blood pressure did not change after intervention. In conclusion, this study highlights the potential efficacy of synbiotic in alleviating pain and improving sleep and quality of life in patients with PDN. papers.title: NAMPT-dependent NAD+ decline drives energy metabolism changes in aging-related atrial fibrillation.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is closely related to aging and involves energy metabolism remodeling. However, the changes in atrial energy metabolism associated with aging-related AF remain unclear. Left atrial appendage samples from AF patients were analyzed for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADtotal) levels using WST-8 method, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content with an ATP detection kit, and silent information regulator sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and protein acetylation levels via western blotting. Aged canine and mouse AF models were created through rapid atrial pacing and intravenous calcium chloride and acetylcholine administration, respectively. An aged cellular AF model was developed using electrical stimulation. Atria or cells from these models were analyzed for the aforementioned parameters. Co-immunoprecipitation in 293T cells verified the interaction between histone arginine methyltransferase 1 (CARM1) and circadian rhythm output cycle protein kaput (CLOCK), and rescue experiments with CARM1 and nicotinamide phosphoribosyl transferase (NAMPT) inhibitors explored their roles in regulating NAD+ and atrial energy metabolism remodeling in AF. Clinical samples showed decreased NADtotal, SIRT1 and ATP levels, validated in aged canine, mouse, and cellular AF models. Cell-level tests revealed that the NAMPT activator P7C3-A20 increased NAD+ levels, while the inhibitor FK866 decreased them. Co-IP experiments indicated an interaction between CARM1 and CLOCK, with CARM1 expression upregulated in AF. Rescue experiments demonstrated that combined CARM1 and NAMPT inhibitors lowered NAD+ levels, suggesting that CARM1 regulates the CLOCK/NAMPT pathway, affecting NAD+ metabolism in AF. CARM1 may influence the CLOCK/NAMPT pathway and may be associated with reduced NADtotal evels, potentially contributing to impaired atrial energy metabolism in aging-related AF.

papers.title: Excessive daytime sleepiness caused by multiple focal strokes in thalamus, hypothalamus, and Edinger-Westphal nucleus: a case report.
papers.abstract: Sleep and wakefulness regulation is mediated by distributed interactions among thalamocortical circuits, hypothalamic orexinergic systems, and brainstem modulatory networks. Although the Edinger-Westphal nucleus is traditionally associated with parasympathetic pupillary control, its potential contribution to sleep and wakefulness regulation remains incompletely understood. We report a case of a 58-year-old male patient with excessive daytime sleepiness, bilateral ptosis with mydriasis (pupil diameter 6.0 mm), and complete loss of both direct and consensual light reflexes. The symptoms of hypersomnia disappeared and 24-hour polysomnography result was partially improved, with exception of still absence of stage 3 non-rapid eye movement sleep one month later. There was no improvement in the symptoms of oculomotor nerve paralysis and mydriasis. Thalamic and hypothalamic lesions can produce severe but partially reversible hypersomnia, likely mediated through disruption of thalamocortical and orexinergic systems. Midbrain involvement results in persistent oculomotor dysfunction. This case highlights the importance of distributed network interactions in sleep and wakefulness regulation and should be interpreted cautiously with regard to the specific role of the Edinger-Westphal nucleus.

papers.title: Effects of an online caregiver respiratory education program on sleep-related outcomes and parental stress in children with neuromuscular diseases: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Children with neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) commonly experience sleep disturbances related to respiratory dysfunction, which may also increase caregiver stress. This study evaluated the effects of a structured caregiver respiratory education program on sleep-related outcomes in children with NMDs and parental stress. A randomized controlled pretest-posttest trial was conducted between December 2023 and April 2024 in Tehran and Isfahan, Iran. Ninety-nine children with NMD and their primary caregivers were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 50) or a control group (n = 49). The intervention group received four 75-minute online educational sessions over two weeks focusing on respiratory care techniques, including diaphragmatic breathing, airway clearance, postural drainage, effective coughing and suctioning, positioning, and basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Attendance was monitored during sessions. The control group received routine hospital-based education. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and two weeks post-intervention using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) and Stress Response Inventory (SRI). No significant between-group differences were observed in the change in total sleep quality (between-group difference = - 0.12, 95% CI: -1.46 to 1.23; P = .286) or parental stress scores (between-group difference = - 0.89, 95% CI: -2.93 to 1.14; P = .871). However, exploratory analyses showed significant improvements in bedtime resistance (P = .01), sleep anxiety (P < .001), and parasomnias (P = .01) in the intervention group compared with the control group. Somatization scores also differed significantly between groups (P = .02), whereas no significant differences were observed for the remaining parental stress domains. Given the multiple subscale comparisons performed, these findings should be considered exploratory and interpreted with caution. Caregiver respiratory education may improve selected sleep-related behaviors in children with neuromuscular diseases and may have beneficial effects on specific dimensions of caregiver stress. Although no significant effects were observed on overall sleep quality or total parental stress, caregiver respiratory education may serve as a complementary rehabilitation approach for families of children with neuromuscular diseases. Further studies with longer follow-up periods and objective sleep outcome measures are needed to confirm these exploratory findings. Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT; IRCT20221231056998N1) registered on April 25, 2023.

papers.title: Parental perception of children sleep pattern changes during FIFA World Cup 2022.
papers.abstract: The circadian clock is an internal, ~ 24-hour biological timer that synchronizes physiology with the day-night cycle. Social jetlag. (SJL) describes the misalignment between this internal clock and social schedules, a condition affecting approximately 70% of the population and linked to a spectrum of metabolic, mental, and cognitive health issues. This study examined how the 2022 FIFA World Cup disrupted normal children's sleep routines and other associated factors from parents' prospect. An online, cross-sectional survey was distributed to parents (N = 848). The questionnaire collected sociodemographic data, children's habitual sleep habits, and changes perceived during the 2022 FIFA World Cup. We operationalized a researcher-defined parent-reported (SJL) as a ≥ 1-hour delay in bedtime on weekends versus weekdays. Multivariable logistic regression analyses identified factors associated with perceived sleep changes and SJL. Over half (53.4%) of the children exhibited a bedtime-based SJL (≥ 1-hour later weekend vs. weekday bedtime). Significant predictors of baseline weekend (SJL) were, children aged 5-11 (84.7% more, p < 0.001), higher socioeconomic status (38.3%, p < 0.001), residency in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia time zone (284.5% times more, p < 0.001). During the tournament, 33% and 17.8% of parents reported their children had delayed sleep timing (≥1 hour) on weekdays and weekends respectively. Regression analysis revealed that parental perceived FIFA impact on their children sleep was significantly associated with weekdays (SJL) 95.8% more, p=0.001 and weekends 78.4% more, p=0.009 during the FIFIA season. Major sporting and social events might significantly disrupt children's sleep schedules, compounding the public health issue of chronic SJL. Such periodic events expose the vulnerability in paediatric population by aggravating already existing SJL. Therefore, families need proactive guidance dealing with such events to protect their children of already existing SJL from baseline social and societal factors, and help them recover from their negative consequences on paediatric circadian biology.

papers.title: Tunnelled intrathecal catheter enabling repeated spinal anaesthesia in MR-Linac radiotherapy: a case report.
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance-guided linear accelerators (MR-Linac) integrate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with radiotherapy delivery, enabling adaptive treatment. However, patient immobility is required for 60-90 min within a high-field magnet, making anaesthetic management challenging. Sedation may be inadequate in patients with opioid tolerance or obstructive sleep apnoea, while general anaesthesia (GA) poses significant risks due to airway and equipment limitations in the MR environment. We present a 78-year-old male with prostate cancer, severe chronic pain, opioid tolerance, and prior spinal instrumentation undergoing 28 MR-Linac sessions. Sedation attempts failed due to persistent involuntary leg movements and apnoea episodes. GA was deemed high-risk due to obesity, obstructive sleep apnoea, chronic opioid and alcohol use, and limited emergency access in the MR-Linac suite. Epidural anaesthesia was unfeasible due to adhesions from prior spinal surgery. A tunnelled intrathecal catheter was placed at the L3-L4 level, enabling daily intermittent spinal anaesthesia with 0.5% bupivacaine. All 28 fractions were completed uneventfully, without infection, neurological deficit, or catheter-related complications. Repeated spinal anaesthesia delivered through a tunnelled intrathecal catheter enabled successful completion of MR-Linac radiotherapy in this carefully selected patient after conventional sedation had failed. This case highlights an individualized management approach for a challenging clinical scenario.

papers.title: Prevalence of Insomnia in the General Population in Pakistan: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a frequent disorder of sleep that is linked to dysfunction and decreased quality of life. However, the burden of this condition at the population level is not known in Pakistan. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence of insomnia in Pakistan. The databases that were searched were PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO and Cochrane Library, in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with the included range in publications from 2018 to 2025. Insomnia prevalence studies in Pakistani population was included. Data were extracted systematically, quality was evaluated according to the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist and pooled prevalence was computed applying a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey transformation. A total of fifteen cross sectional studies with 7287 individuals were included. Insomnia prevalence ranged from 17.2% to 72.0%, with a pooled prevalence of 51% (95% CI: 44-58%). There was significant heterogeneity (I² = 97%, p < 0.001), which may have resulted from different populations, different regions, different sampling and assessment techniques. A higher prevalence was noted among young adults (18-29 years, 55%) and studies conducted with the use of the Insomnia Severity Index (54%). Common factors associated with psychological stress were anxiety, depression, excessive internet usage, social media usage, and irregular sleep patterns. Insomnia is a major public health problem in Pakistan especially in the younger age groups. Enhancement of screening, awareness and evidence-based interventions are required. National representative studies with standard diagnostic criteria are recommended in the future.

papers.title: Sleep-sensitive neurons mediate consolidation.
Endogenous rhythms in deep-sea mussel cell culture and molecular clock characterization.
papers.abstract: While biological rhythms are crucial to life, the deep sea has long been considered an arrhythmic exception. However, at hydrothermal vents - devoid of diel cues yet shaped by tides - the mussel Bathymodiolus azoricus shows both tidal and, unexpectedly, circadian rhythms at -1700 m. Whether endogenous clock(s) drive these cycles remained unanswered. Here, we report endogenous circadian rhythms in B. azoricus cell cultures under constant conditions: isolated cells display a circadian oscillation despite tidal-dominant rhythms in the natural environment. Reporter assays using genomic regions upstream of the mussel's per gene and containing E-box motifs suggest that a functional transcription-translation feedback loop (TTFL) contributes to circadian timing even in the deep sea. In mussels, BazPeriod lacks autonomous repressive activity but modulates BazCry2. As BazPeriod itself oscillates tidally, it may explain how a single endogenous clock yields both tidal and diel rhythms. The work also spotlights the highly time-sensitive biology of the vastly unexplored deep-sea environment.

papers.title: Clinical, neuroimaging, and longitudinal progression characteristics of GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease in a Northeast China cohort.
papers.abstract: GBA1 is a common genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease (PD), but PET/CT and longitudinal data in Chinese populations remain limited. We aimed to determine the frequency of GBA1-associated PD (GBA1-PD) in Northeast China and compare its clinical features, PET/CT images, and 3-year progression with non-GBA1-associated PD (NGBA1-PD). In this single-center observational cohort, 301 patients with PD underwent whole-exome sequencing, orthogonal validation and clinical assessment; 176 underwent 11C-CFT and 18F-FDG PET/CT, and 271 completed follow-up. GBA1 variants were identified in 25 patients (8.31%). Compared with NGBA1-PD, GBA1-PD showed greater motor and cognitive impairment, higher PIGD proportion, worse sleep-related symptoms, lower striatal 11C-CFT uptake, and lower metabolism in the precuneus. Over 3 years, GBA1-PD showed trends toward faster motor and mood deterioration, although these differences did not remain significant after FDR correction. These findings suggest distinct clinical and imaging features of GBA1-PD and potential value for prognostic stratification. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

papers.title: Adolescent environmental enrichment prevents early-life stress-induced schizophrenia-like phenotypes via restoration of CREB-BDNF-TrkB signaling.
papers.abstract: Early-life stress (ELS) is a major environmental risk factor for schizophrenia, yet effective preventive strategies targeting its neurodevelopmental consequences remain limited. Here, we show that adolescent environmental enrichment (EE) prevents the emergence of schizophrenia-like behavioral and cognitive deficits induced by maternal separation (MS), a validated ELS model. Mechanistically, MS induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and synaptic deficits in the hippocampus, accompanied by suppression of the CREB-BDNF-TrkB (cAMP response element-binding protein-brain-derived neurotrophic factor-tropomyosin receptor kinase B) signaling. Adolescent EE robustly reversed these abnormalities and restored neuroplasticity-related signaling. Importantly, we provide evidence supporting a causal role of TrkB signaling in these protective effects within the experimental framework used here: pharmacological activation of TrkB rescued oxidative stress-induced synaptic deficits in vitro, whereas pharmacological inhibition of TrkB abolished the behavioral and cognitive benefits of EE in vivo. To establish translational relevance, we further show that TrkB levels are significantly reduced in neuron-derived exosomes (NDEs) from patients with schizophrenia, with moderate diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.784). Together, these findings support CREB-BDNF-TrkB signaling as a key mechanistic node linking ELS to schizophrenia-related phenotypes and suggest adolescent EE as a developmentally timed, non-pharmacological intervention with translational relevance within the experimental framework used here.

papers.title: The quiet end of the spectrum: A case report and review of "simple schizophrenia".
papers.abstract: BackgroundSchizophrenia is increasingly understood as a neurodevelopmental disorder in which cognitive and negative symptoms may precede or overshadow florid psychosis. Such neuropsychiatric presentations can be difficult to recognise within current diagnostic frameworks that privilege positive symptoms.ObjectiveTo illustrate a schizophrenia presentation without hallucinations and delusions and to contextualise it within contemporary and historical nosology.MethodsSingle case report with a focussed narrative review of the literature on simple schizophrenia subtypes.Casea 24-year-old woman experienced a two-year insidious decline in motivation, social engagement, and cognition, with prominent affective flattening, avolition, bradyphrenia, poverty of speech, and psychomotor slowing. There were no delusions or hallucinations, and thought form was linear. Extensive investigations including MRI, EEG, FDG-PET, and CSF studies were unremarkable. Neuropsychological testing showed deficits in new learning, processing speed, and executive functioning consistent with schizophrenia-spectrum illness. The illness was refractory to multiple antidepressants, antipsychotics, and a course of electroconvulsive therapy. Following exclusion of organic pathology, multidisciplinary assessment, and longitudinal review, a diagnosis of schizophrenia was formulated.ConclusionCurrent diagnostic systems may overlook individuals with schizophrenia without hallucinations or delusions. Incorporating neuropsychiatric markers and establishing cognitive trajectories into diagnostic thinking may enable earlier identification and more targeted interventions.

papers.title: Effectiveness of a Socioecological School-Based 24-h Movement Behaviour Intervention on Lifestyle Behaviours Among Children and Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity: A Gender-Stratified Quasi-Experimental Study.
papers.abstract: Childhood obesity and inadequate physical activity are major public health concerns in Pakistan. Evidence on multicomponent school-based interventions targeting 24-h movement behaviours, particularly with gender-specific approaches, remains limited. A 12-week quasi-experimental cluster-controlled study was conducted in eight public schools in Lahore, Pakistan. A total of 1200 children and adolescents (577 boys, 623 girls; aged 9-17 years) were assigned to an intervention group (n = 570) or a control group (n = 630). The intervention, guided by the socioecological model, included enhanced physical education, extracurricular physical activity, health education, parental engagement and supportive school environments. Outcomes included anthropometric measures and 24-h movement behaviours. Intervention effects were analysed using repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) and general linear mixed models (p < 0.05). Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for physical activity (η2 = 0.28), screen time (η2 = 0.15), sleep duration (η2 = 0.16) and fast-food consumption (η2 = 0.07) (all p < 0.001). The prevalence of overweight and obesity among children and adolescents declined from 31.0% to 28.0% in the intervention group but increased from 36.0% to 38.0% in the control group (p = 0.005). Physical activity guideline adherence increased from 26.3% to 71.8% among boys and from 22.2% to 63.3% among girls (both p < 0.001). Significant reductions in BMI, waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio were also observed in the intervention group. A multicomponent, socioecological, school-based intervention effectively improved movement behaviours, dietary habits, parental support and outcomes related to overweight and obesity among Pakistani children and adolescents. These findings support integrated school- and family-based strategies for preventing childhood obesity across both boys and girls.

papers.title: Medicating inhibitory control? Treatment with serotonergic antidepressants predicts stop-N200 amplitudes in major depressive disorder.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent chronic mental illness often treated by serotonergic pharmacotherapy and complicated by sex differences and comorbid anxiety disorders (COMs). Deficits in inhibitory control are a transdiagnostic feature of MDD and COM, though the presentation of these deficits may be impacted by competing cognitive demands, symptoms severity, sexes, and medication status. This project includes 233 participants from the Tulsa 1000 study who completed concurrent electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic functional resonance imaging (MRI) during a stop signal task (SST). We examined how serotonergic antidepressants, biological sex, and comorbidity with an anxiety disorder uniquely relate to neural indices of inhibitory control for healthy controls (HCs), MDD, and COM using linear mixed effect models, type III ANOVAs, and optimal full propensity matching. N200, P300, and correct-related negativity (CRN) components were extracted and analyzed to index conflict monitoring, conflict resolution, and performance monitoring, respectively, in response to stop signals and their absence. Our results revealed that HCs exhibited larger stop-P300 amplitudes than MDD and COM (η2 = 0.068); females had smaller stop-N200 amplitudes than males (η2 = 0.027); MDD/COM participants taking a serotonergic antidepressant exhibited less negative N200 amplitudes than those who were not (LME, B = 1.95; η2 = 0.044; ATE, B = 2.47). Our findings suggest being treated with serotonergic antidepressants are associated with neural differences in the conflict monitoring of inhibitory control in pure and comorbid depression.
